verses.1: The LORD also spake unto Joshua, saying,
verses.2: Speak to the children of Israel, saying, Appoint out for you cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses:
verses.3: That the slayer that killeth any person unawares and unwittingly may flee thither: and they shall be your refuge from the avenger of blood.
verses.4: And when he that doth flee unto one of those cities shall stand at the entering of the gate of the city, and shall declare his cause in the ears of the elders of that city, they shall take him into the city unto them, and give him a place, that he may dwell among them.
verses.5: And if the avenger of blood pursue after him, then they shall not deliver the slayer up into his hand; because he smote his neighbour unwittingly, and hated him not beforetime.
verses.6: And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, and until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.
verses.7: ¶ And they appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, and Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah.
verses.8: And on the other side Jordan by Jericho eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness upon the plain out of the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.
verses.9: These were the cities appointed for all the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation.

verses.3: Φυγαδευτήριον τῷ φονευτῇ τῷ πατάξαντι ψυχὴν ἀκουσίως· καὶ ἔσονται ὑμῖν αἱ πόλεις φυγαδευτήριον, καὶ οὐκ ἀποθανεῖται ὁ φονευτὴς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγχιστεύοντος τὸ αἷμα, ἕως ἂν καταστῇ· ἐναντίον τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰς κρίσιν.
verses.7: Καὶ διέστειλε τὴν Κάδης ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Νεφθαλὶ, καὶ Συχὲμ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Ἐφραὶμ, καὶ τὴν πόλιν Ἀρβὸκ, αὕτη ἐστὶ Χεβρὼν, ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Ἰούδα.
verses.8: Καὶ ἐν τῷ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ἔδωκε Βοσὸρ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ ἀπὸ τῆς φυλῆς Ῥουβὴν, καὶ Ἀρημὼθ ἐν τῇ Γαλαὰδ ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Γὰδ, καὶ τὴν Γαυλὼν ἐν τῇ Βασανίτιδι ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Μανασσῆ.
verses.9: Αὗται αἱ πόλεις αἱ ἐπίκλητοι τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ καὶ τῷ προσηλύτῳ τῷ προσκειμένῳ ἐν αὐτοῖς, καταφυγεῖν ἐκεῖ παντὶ παίοντι ψυχὴν ἀκουσίως, ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνῃ ἐν χειρὶ τοῦ ἀγχιστεύοντος τὸ αἷμα, ἕως ἄν καταστῇ ἔναντι τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰς κρίσιν.

verses.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
verses.2: If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?
verses.3: Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.
verses.4: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.
verses.5: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
verses.6: Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?
verses.7: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?
verses.8: Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.
verses.9: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.
verses.10: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
verses.11: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion’s whelps are scattered abroad.
verses.12: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.
verses.13: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,
verses.14: Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake.
verses.15: Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:
verses.16: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,
verses.17: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?
verses.18: Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly:
verses.19: How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?
verses.20: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it.
verses.21: Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἐλιφὰς ὁ Θαιμανίτης, λέγει,
verses.2: Μὴ πολλάκις σοι λελάληται ἐν κόπῳ; ἰσχὺν δὲ ῥημάτων σου τίς ὑποίσει;
verses.3: Εἰ γὰρ σὺ ἐνουθέτησας πολλοὺς, καὶ χεῖρας ἀσθενοῦς παρεκάλεσας,
verses.4: ἀσθενοῦντάς τε ἐξανέστησας ῥήμασι, γόνασί τε ἀδυνατοῦσι θάρσος περιέθηκας.
verses.5: Νῦν δὲ ἥκει ἐπὶ σὲ πόνος καὶ ἥψατό σου, σὺ ἐσπούδασας.
verses.6: Πότερον οὐχ ὁ φόβος σου ἐστὶν ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ, καὶ ἡ ἐλπίς σου καὶ ἡ κακία τῆς ὁδοῦ σου;
verses.7: Μνήσθητι οὖν, τίς καθαρὸς ὢν ἀπώλετο, ἢ πότε ἀληθινοὶ ὁλόῤῥιζοι ἀπώλοντο;
verses.8: Καθʼ ὃν τρόπον εἶδον τοὺς ἀροτριῶντας τὰ ἄτοπα, οἱ δὲ σπείροντες αὐτὰ ὀδύνας θεριοῦσιν ἑαυτοῖς.
verses.9: Ἀπὸ προστάγματος Κυρίου ἀπολοῦνται, ἀπὸ δὲ πνεύματος ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ ἀφανισθήσονται.
verses.10: Σθένος λέοντος, φωνὴ δὲ λεαίνης, γαυρίαμα δὲ δρακόντων ἐσβέσθη.
verses.11: Μυρμηκολέων ὤλετο παρὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βορὰν, σκύμνοι δὲ λεόντων ἔλιπον ἀλλήλους.
verses.12: Εἰ δέ τι ῥῆμα ἀληθινὸν ἐγεγόνει ἐν λόγοις σου, οὐθὲν ἄν σοι τούτων κακὸν ἀπήντησε· πότερον οὐ δέξεταί μου τὸ οὖς ἐξαίσια παρʼ αὐτοῦ;
verses.13: Φόβῳ δὲ καὶ ἤχῳ νυκτερινῇ ἐπιπίπτων φόβος ἐπʼ ἀνθρώπους,
verses.14: φρίκη μοι συνήντησεν καὶ τρόμος, καὶ μεγάλως μου τὰ ὀστᾶ διέσεισε,
verses.15: καὶ πνεῦμα ἐπὶ πρόσωπόν μου ἐπῆλθεν, ἔφριξαν δέ μου τρίχες καὶ σάρκες.
verses.16: Ἀνέστην καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνων, εἶδον καὶ οὐκ ἦν μορφὴ πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν μου, ἀλλʼ ἢ αὖραν καὶ φωνὴν ἤκουον.
verses.17: Τί γάρ; μὴ καθαρὸς ἔσται βροτὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ Κυρίου; ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ἄμεμπτος ἀνήρ;
verses.18: Εἰ κατὰ παίδων αὐτοῦ οὐ πιστεύει, κατὰ δὲ ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ σκολιόν τι ἐπενόησε.
verses.19: Τοὺς δὲ κατοικοῦντας οἰκίας πηλίνας, ἐξ ὧν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ πηλοῦ ἐσμεν, ἔπαισεν αὐτοὺς σητὸς τρόπον,
verses.20: καὶ ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν μέχρι ἑσπέρας οὐκ ἔτι εἰσὶ, παρὰ τὸ μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς ἑαυτοῖς βοηθῆσαι, ἀπώλοντο.
verses.21: Ἐνεφύσησε γὰρ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐξηράνθησαν, ἀπώλοντο παρὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν αὐτοὺς σοφίαν.

verses.1: Then Eliphaz the Thæmanite answered and said,
verses.2: Hast thou been often spoken to in distress? but who shall endure the force of thy words?
verses.3: For whereas thou hast instructed many, and hast strengthened the hands of the weak one,
verses.4: and hast supported the failing with words, and hast imparted courage to feeble knees.
verses.5: Yet now that pain has come upon thee, and touched thee, thou art troubled.
verses.6: Is not thy fear founded in folly, thy hope also, and the mischief of thy way?
verses.7: Remember then who has perished, being pure? or when were the true-hearted utterly destroyed?
verses.8: Accordingly as I have seen men ploughing barren places, and they that sow them will reap sorrows for themselves.
verses.9: They shall perish by the command of the Lord, and shall be utterly consumed by the breath of his wrath.
verses.10: The strength of the lion, and the voice of the lioness, and the exulting cry of serpents are quenched.
verses.11: The old lion has perished for want of food, and the lions' whelps have forsaken one another.
verses.12: But if there had been any truth in thy words, none of these evils would have befallen thee. Shall not mine ear receive excellent revelations from him?
verses.13: But as when terror falls upon men, with dread and a sound in the night,
verses.14: horror and trembling seized me, and caused all my bones greatly to shake.
verses.15: And a spirit came before my face; and my hair and flesh quivered.
verses.16: I arose and perceived it not: I looked, and there was no form before my eyes: but I only heard a breath and a voice, saying,
verses.17: What, shall a mortal be pure before the Lord? or a man be blameless in regard to his works?
verses.18: Whereas he trusts not in his servants, and perceives perverseness in his angels.
verses.19: But as for them that dwell in houses of clay, of whom we also are formed of the same clay, he smites them like a moth.
verses.20: And from morning to evening they no longer exist: they have perished, because they cannot help themselves.
verses.21: For he blows upon them, and they are withered: they have perished for lack of wisdom.

verses.1: Call now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?
verses.2: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.
verses.3: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
verses.4: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them.
verses.5: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance.
verses.6: Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;
verses.7: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
verses.8: I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:
verses.9: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:
verses.10: Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields:
verses.11: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.
verses.12: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.
verses.13: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.
verses.14: They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.
verses.15: But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.
verses.16: So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.
verses.17: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:
verses.18: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.
verses.19: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.
verses.20: In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.
verses.21: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.
verses.22: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
verses.23: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
verses.24: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.
verses.25: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.
verses.26: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.
verses.27: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.

verses.1: Ἐπικαλέσαι δὲ εἴ τις σοι ὑπακούσεται, ἢ εἴ τινα ἀγγέλων ἁγίων ὄψῃ·
verses.2: Καὶ γὰρ ἄφρονα ἀναιρεῖ ὀργὴ, πεπλανημένον δὲ θανατοῖ ζῆλος.
verses.3: Ἐγὼ δὲ ἑώρακα ἄφρονας ῥίζαν βάλλοντας, ἀλλʼ εὐθέως ἐβρώθη αὐτῶν ἡ δίαιτα.
verses.4: Πόῤῥω γένοιντο οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ σωτηρίας, κολαβρισθείησαν δὲ ἐπὶ θύραις ἡσσόνων, καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ ἐξαιρούμενος.
verses.5: Ἃ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι συνήγαγον, δίκαιοι ἔδονται, αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐκ κακῶν οὐκ ἐξαίρετοι ἔσονται· ἐκσιφωνισθείη αὐτῶν ἡ ἰσχύς.
verses.6: Οὐ γὰρ μὴ ἐξέλθῃ ἐκ τῆς γῆς κόπος, οὐδὲ ἐξ ὀρέων ἀναβλαστήσει πόνος.
verses.7: Ἀλλὰ ἄνθρωπος γεννᾶται κόπῳ, νεοσσοὶ δὲ γυπὸς τὰ ὑψηλὰ πέτονται.
verses.8: Οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ ἐγὼ δεηθήσομαι Κυρίου, Κύριον δὲ τὸν πάντων δεσπότην ἐπικαλέσομαι,
verses.9: τὸν ποιοῦντα μεγάλα καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστα, ἔνδοξά τε καὶ ἐξαίσια, ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμὸς,
verses.10: τὸν διδόντα ὑετὸν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, ἀποστέλλοντα ὕδωρ ἐπὶ τὴν ὑπʼ οὐρανὸν,
verses.11: τὸν ποιοῦντα ταπεινοὺς εἰς ὕψος, καὶ ἀπολωλότας ἐξεγείροντα,
verses.12: διαλλάσσοντα βουλὰς πανούργων, καὶ οὐ μὴ ποιήσουσιν αἱ χεῖρες αὐτῶν ἀληθές·
verses.13: ὁ καταλαμβάνων σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ φρονήσει, βουλὴν δὲ πολυπλόκων ἐξέστησεν.
verses.14: Ἡμέρας συναντήσεται αὐτοῖς σκότος, τὸ δὲ μεσημβρινὸν ψηλαφήσαισαν ἶσα νυκτὶ,
verses.15: ἀπόλοιντο δὲ ἐν πολέμῳ· ἀδύνατος δὲ ἐξέλθοι ἐκ χειρὸς δυνάστου.
verses.16: Εἴη δὲ ἀδυνάτῳ ἐλπὶς, ἀδίκου δὲ στόμα ἐμφραχθείη.
verses.17: Μακάριος δὲ ἄνθρωπος ὃν ἤλεγξεν ὁ Κύριος, νουθέτημα δὲ παντοκράτορος μὴ ἀπαναίνου.
verses.18: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀλγεῖν ποιεῖ, καὶ πάλιν ἀποκαθίστησιν· ἔπαισε, καὶ αἱ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ ἰάσαντο.
verses.19: Ἑξάκις ἐξ ἀναγκῶν σε ἐξελεῖται, ἐν δὲ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ οὐ μὴ ἅψηταί σου κακόν.
verses.20: Ἐν λιμῷ ῥύσεταί σε ἐκ θανάτου, ἐν πολέμῳ δὲ ἐκ χειρὸς σιδήρου λύσει σε.
verses.21: Ἀπὸ μάστιγος γλώσσης σε κρύψει, καὶ οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇς ἀπὸ κακῶν ἐρχομένων.
verses.22: Ἀδίκων καὶ ἀνόμων καταγελάσῃ· ἀπὸ δὲ θηρίων ἀγρίων οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇς·
verses.23: Θῆρες γὰρ ἄγριοι εἰρηνεύσουσί σοι.
verses.24: Εἶτα γνώσῃ ὅτι εἰρηνεύσει σου ὁ οἶκος· ἡ δὲ δίαιτα τῆς σκηνῆς σου οὐ μὴ ἁμάρτῃ.
verses.25: Γνώσῃ δὲ ὅτι πολὺ τὸ σπέρμα σου, τὰ δὲ τέκνα σου ἔσται ὥσπερ τὸ παμβότανον τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
verses.26: Ἐλεύσῃ δὲ ἐν τάφῳ ὥσπερ σῖτος ὥριμος κατὰ καιρὸν θεριζόμενος, ἢ ὥσπερ θιμωνία ἅλωνος καθʼ ὥραν συγκομισθεῖσα.
verses.27: Ἰδοὺ ταῦτα οὕτως ἐξιχνιάσαμεν· ταῦτά ἐστιν ἃ ἀκηκόαμεν· σὺ δὲ γνῶθι σεαυτῷ, εἴ τι ἔπραξας.

verses.1: But call, if any one will hearken to thee, or if thou shalt see any of the holy angels.
verses.2: For wrath destroys the foolish one, and envy slays him that has gone astray.
verses.3: And I have seen foolish ones taking root: but suddenly their habitation was devoured.
verses.4: Let their children be far from safety, and let them be crushed at the doors of vile men, and let there be no deliverer.
verses.5: For what they have collected, the just shall eat; but they shall not be delivered out of calamities: let their strength be utterly exhausted.
verses.6: For labour cannot by any means come out of the earth, nor shall trouble spring out of the mountains:
verses.7: yet man is born to labour, and even so the vulture's young seek the high places.
verses.8: Nevertheless I will beseech the Lord, and will call upon the Lord, the sovereign of all;
verses.9: who does great things and untraceable, glorious things also, and marvellous, of which there is no number:
verses.10: who gives rain upon the earth, sending water on the earth:
verses.11: who exalts the lowly, and raises up them that are lost:
verses.12: frustrating the counsels of the crafty, and their hands shall not perform the truth:
verses.13: who takes the wise in their wisdom, and subverts the counsel of the crafty.
verses.14: In the day darkness shall come upon them, and let them grope in the noon-day even as in the night:
verses.15: and let them perish in war, and let the weak escape from the hand of the mighty.
verses.16: And let the weak have hope, but the mouth of the unjust be stopped.
verses.17: But blessed is the man whom the Lord has reproved; and reject not thou the chastening of the Almighty.
verses.18: For he causes a man to be in pain, and restores him again: he smites, and his hands heal.
verses.19: Six times he shall deliver thee out of distresses: and in the seventh harm shall not touch thee.
verses.20: In famine he shall deliver thee from death: and in war he shall free thee from the power of the sword.
verses.21: He shall hide thee from the scourge of the tongue: and thou shalt not be afraid of coming evils.
verses.22: Thou shalt laugh at the unrighteous and the lawless: and thou shalt not be afraid of wild beasts.
verses.23: For the wild beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
verses.24: Then shalt thou know that thy house shall be at peace, and the provision for thy tabernacle shall not fail.
verses.25: And thou shalt know that thy seed shall be abundant; and thy children shall be like the herbage of the field.
verses.26: And thou shalt come to the grave like ripe corn reaped in its season, or as a heap of the corn-flour collected in proper time.
verses.27: Behold, we have thus sought out these matters; these are what we have heard: but do thou reflect with thyself, if thou hast done anything wrong.

verses.1: Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?
verses.2: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work:
verses.3: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.
verses.4: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
verses.5: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.
verses.6: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
verses.7: O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.
verses.8: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.
verses.9: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.
verses.10: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
verses.11: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.12: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?
verses.13: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;
verses.14: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions:
verses.15: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.
verses.16: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.
verses.17: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?
verses.18: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?
verses.19: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
verses.20: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?
verses.21: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.

verses.1: Πότερον οὐχὶ πειρατήριόν ἐστιν ὁ βίος ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς; καὶ ὥσπερ μισθίου αὐθημερινοῦ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ;
verses.2: Ἢ ὥσπερ θεράπων δεδοικὼς τὸν Κύριον αὐτοῦ, καὶ τετευχὼς σκιᾶς; ἢ ὥσπερ μισθωτὸς ἀναμένων τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ;
verses.3: Οὕτως κᾀγὼ ὑπέμεινα μῆνας κενοὺς, νύκτες δὲ ὀδυνῶν δεδομέναι μοι εἰσίν.
verses.4: Ἐὰν κοιμηθῶ, λέγω, πότε ἡμέρα; ὡς δʼ ἂν ἀναστῶ, πάλιν, πότε ἑσπέρα; πλήρης δὲ γίνομαι ὀδυνῶν ἀπὸ ἑσπέρας ἕως πρωΐ.
verses.5: Φύρεται δέ μου τὸ σῶμα ἐν σαπρίᾳ σκωλήκων, τήκω δὲ βώλακας γῆς ἀπὸ ἰχῶρος ξύων.
verses.6: Ὁ δὲ βίος μου ἔστιν ἐλαφρότερος λαλιᾶς, ἀπόλωλε δὲ ἐν κενῇ ἐλπίδι.
verses.7: Μνήσθητι οὖν ὅτι πνεῦμά μου ἡ ζωὴ, καὶ οὐκ ἔτι ἐπανελεύσεται ὀφθαλμός μου ἰδεῖν ἀγαθόν.
verses.8: Οὐ περιβλέψεταί με ὀφθαλμὸς ὁρῶντός με, οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου ἐν ἐμοί, καὶ οὐκ ἔτι εἰμί·
verses.9: Ὥσπερ νέφος ἀποκαθαρθὲν ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ· ἐὰν γὰρ ἄνθρωπος καταβῇ εἰς ᾅδην, οὐκ ἔτι μὴ ἀναβῇ,
verses.10: οὐδʼ οὐ μὴ ἐπιστρέψῃ εἰς τὸν ἴδιον οἶκον, οὐδʼ οὐ μὴ ἐπιγνῶ αὐτὸν ἔτι ὁ τόπος αὐτοῦ.
verses.11: Ἀτὰρ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐγὼ φείσομαι τῷ στόματί μου, λαλήσω ἐν ἀνάγκῃ ὤν, ἀνοίξω πικρίαν ψυχῆς μου συνεχόμενος.
verses.12: Πότερον θάλασσα εἰμὶ ἢ δράκων, ὅτι κατέταξας ἐπʼ ἐμὲ φυλακήν;

verses.14: Ἐκφοβεῖς με ἐνυπνίοις, καὶ ὁράμασί με καταπλήσσεις.
verses.15: Ἀπαλλάξεις ἀπὸ πνεύματός μου τὴν ψυχήν μου, ἀπὸ δὲ θανάτου τὰ ὀστᾶ μου.
verses.16: Οὐ γὰρ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ζήσομαι, ἵνα μακροθυμήσω· ἀπόστα ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, κενὸς γάρ μου ὁ βίος.
verses.17: Τί γάρ ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος, ὅτι ἐμεγάλυνας αὐτόν; ἢ ὅτι προσέχεις τὸν νοῦν εἰς αὐτόν;
verses.18: Ἢ ἐπισκοπὴν αὐτοῦ ποιήσῃ ἕως τὸ πρωΐ; καὶ εἰς ἀνάπαυσιν αὐτὸν κρινεῖς;
verses.19: Ἕως τίνος οὐκ ἐᾷς με, οὐδὲ προΐῃ με, ἕως ἂν καταπίω τὸν πτύελόν μου;
verses.20: Εἰ ἐγὼ ἥμαρτον, τί δυνήσομαι πρᾶξαι, ὁ ἐπιστάμενος τὸν νοῦν τῶν ἀνθρώπων; διατί ἔθου με κατεντευκτήν σου, εἰμὶ δὲ ἐπὶ σοὶ φορτίον;
verses.21: Διατί οὐκ ἐποιήσω τῆς ἀνομίας μου λήθην, καὶ καθαρισμὸν τῆς ἁμαρτίας μου; νυνὶ δὲ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσομαι, ὀρθρίζων δὲ οὐκ ἔτι εἰμί.

verses.1: Is not the life of man upon earth a state of trial? and his existence as that of a hireling by the day?
verses.2: Or as a servant that fears his master, and one who has grasped a shadow? or as a hireling waiting for his pay?
verses.3: So have I also endured months of vanity, and nights of pain have been appointed me.
verses.4: Whenever I lie down, I say, When will it be day? and whenever I rise up, again I say when will it be evening? and I am full of pains from evening to morning.
verses.5: And my body is covered with loathsome worms; and I waste away, scraping off clods of dust from my eruption.
verses.6: And my life is lighter than a word, and has perished in vain hope.
verses.7: Remember then that my life is breath, and mine eye shall not yet again see good.
verses.8: The eye of him that sees me shall not see me again: thine eyes are upon me, and I am no more.
verses.9: I am as a cloud that is cleared away from the sky: for if a man go down to the grave, he shall not come up again:
verses.10: and he shall surely not return to his own house, neither shall his place know him any more.
verses.11: Then neither will I refrain my mouth: I will speak being in distress; being in anguish I will disclose the bitterness of my soul.
verses.12: Am I a sea, or a serpent, that thou hast set a watch over me?
verses.13: I said that my bed should comfort me, and I would privately counsel with myself on my couch.
verses.14: Thou scarest me with dreams, and dost terrify me with visions.
verses.15: Thou wilt separate life from my spirit; and yet keep my bones from death.
verses.16: For I shall not live for ever, that I should patiently endure: depart from me, for my life is vain.
verses.17: For what is man, that thou hast magnified him? or that thou givest heed to him?
verses.18: Wilt thou visit him till the morning, and judge him till the time of rest?
verses.19: How long dost thou not let me alone, nor let me go, until I shall swallow down my spittle?
verses.20: If I have sinned, what shall I be able to do, O thou that understandest the mind of men? why hast thou made me as thine accuser, and why am I a burden to thee?
verses.21: Why hast thou not forgotten my iniquity, and purged my sin? but now I shall depart to the earth; and in the morning, I am no more.

verses.1: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
verses.2: How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?
verses.3: Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?
verses.4: If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;
verses.5: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;
verses.6: If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
verses.7: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.
verses.8: For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:
verses.9: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)
verses.10: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?
verses.11: Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?
verses.12: Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb.
verses.13: So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish:
verses.14: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.
verses.15: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.
verses.16: He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.
verses.17: His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones.
verses.18: If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.
verses.19: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.
verses.20: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers:
verses.21: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing.
verses.22: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Βαλδὰδ ὁ Σαυχίτης, λέγει,
verses.2: Μέχρι τίνος λαλήσεις ταῦτα, πνεῦμα πολυῤῥῆμον τοῦ στόματός σου;
verses.3: Μὴ ὁ Κύριος ἀδικήσει κρίνων; ἢ ὁ τὰ πάντα ποιήσας ταράξει τὸ δίκαιον;
verses.4: Εἰ οἱ υἱοί σου ἥμαρτον ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ, ἀπέστειλεν ἐν χειρὶ ἀνομίας αὐτῶν.
verses.5: Σὺ δὲ ὄρθριζε πρὸς Κύριον παντοκράτορα δεόμενος.
verses.6: Εἰ καθαρὸς εἶ καὶ ἀληθινὸς, δεήσεως ἐπακούσεταί σου, ἀποκαταστήσει δέ σοι δίαιταν δικαιοσύνης.
verses.7: Ἔσται οὖν τὰ μὲν πρῶτά σου ὀλίγα, τὰ δὲ ἔσχατά σου ἀμύθητα.
verses.8: Ἐπερώτησον γὰρ γενεὰν πρώτην, ἐξιχνίασον δὲ κατὰ γένος πατέρων·
verses.9: Χθιζοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν, καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν· σκιὰ γάρ ἐστιν ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὁ βίος·
verses.10: Ἢ οὐχ οὗτοί σε διδάξουσιν καὶ ἀναγγελοῦσι, καὶ ἐκ καρδίας ἐξάξουσι ῥήματα;
verses.11: Μὴ θάλλει πάπυρος ἄνευ ὕδατος, ἢ ὑψωθήσεται βούτομον ἄνευ πότου;
verses.12: Ἔτι ὂν ἐπὶ ῥίζης, καὶ οὐ μὴ θερισθῇ, πρὸ τοῦ πιεῖν πᾶσα βοτάνη οὐχὶ ξηραίνεται;
verses.13: Οὕτως τοίνυν ἔσται τὰ ἔσχατα πάντων τῶν ἐπιλανθανομένων τοῦ Κυρίου· ἐλπὶς γὰρ ἀσεβοῦς ἀπολεῖται·
verses.14: Ἀοίκητος γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἔσται ὁ οἶκος· ἀράχνη δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀποβήσεται ἡ σκηνή.
verses.15: Ἐὰν ὑπερείσῃ τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ, οὐ μὴ στῇ· ἐπιλαβομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ, οὐ μὴ ὑπομείνῃ·
verses.16: Ὑγρὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὑπὸ ἡλίου· καὶ ἐκ σαπρίας αὐτοῦ ὁ ῥάδαμνος αὐτοῦ ἐξελεύσεται.

verses.19: ὅτι καταστροφὴ ἀσεβοῦς τοιαύτη, ἐκ δὲ γῆς ἄλλον ἀναβλαστήσει.
verses.20: Ὁ γὰρ Κύριος οὐ μὴ ἀποποιήσηται τὸν ἄκακον· πᾶν δὲ δῶρον ἀσεβοῦς οὐ δέξεται.
verses.21: Ἀληθινῶν δὲ στόμα ἐμπλήσει γέλωτος, τὰ δὲ χείλη αὐτῶν ἐξομολογήσεως.
verses.22: Οἱ δὲ ἐχθροὶ αὐτῶν ἐνδύσονται αἰσχύνην, δίαιτα δὲ ἀσεβοῦς οὐκ ἔσται.

verses.1: Then Baldad the Sauchite answered, and said,
verses.2: How long wilt thou speak these things, how long shall the breath of thy mouth be abundant in words?
verses.3: Will the Lord be unjust when he judges; or will he that has made all things pervert justice?
verses.4: If thy sons have sinned before him, he has cast them away because of their transgression.
verses.5: But be thou early in prayer to the Lord Almighty.
verses.6: If thou art pure and true, he will hearken to thy supplication, and will restore to thee the habitation of righteousness.
verses.7: Though then thy beginning should be small, yet thy end should be unspeakably great.
verses.8: For ask of the former generation, and search diligently among the race of our fathers:
verses.9: (for we are of yesterday, and know nothing; for our life upon the earth is a shadow:)
verses.10: shall not these teach thee, and report to thee, and bring out words from their heart?
verses.11: Does the rush flourish without water, or shall the flag grow up without moisture?
verses.12: When it is yet on the root, and though it has not been cut down, does not any herb wither before it has received moisture?
verses.13: Thus then shall be the end of all that forget the Lord: for the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
verses.14: For his house shall be without inhabitants, and his tent shall prove a spider's web.
verses.15: If he should prop up his house, it shall not stand: and when he has taken hold of it, it shall not remain.
verses.16: For it is moist under the sun, and his branch shall come forth out of his dung-heap.
verses.17: He lies down upon a gathering of stones, and shall live in the midst of flints.
verses.18: If God should destroy him, his place shall deny him. Hast thou not seen such things,
verses.19: that such is the overthrow of the ungodly? and out of the earth another shall grow.
verses.20: For the Lord will by no means reject the harmless man; but he will not receive any gift of the ungodly.
verses.21: But he will fill with laughter the mouth of the sincere, and their lips with thanksgiving.
verses.22: But their adversaries shall clothe themselves with shame; and the habitation of the ungodly shall perish.

verses.1: Then Job answered and said,
verses.2: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?
verses.3: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.
verses.4: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?
verses.5: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.
verses.6: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.
verses.7: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.
verses.8: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.
verses.9: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.
verses.10: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.
verses.11: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.
verses.12: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?
verses.13: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.
verses.14: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?
verses.15: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.
verses.16: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.
verses.17: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.
verses.18: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.
verses.19: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?
verses.20: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.
verses.21: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.
verses.22: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
verses.23: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.
verses.24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?
verses.25: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.
verses.26: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.
verses.27: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:
verses.28: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.
verses.29: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?
verses.30: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;
verses.31: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.
verses.32: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.
verses.33: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.
verses.34: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:
verses.35: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἰὼβ, λέγει,

verses.9: Ὁ ποιῶν Πλειάδα καὶ Ἕσπερον καὶ Ἀρκτοῦρον, καὶ ταμεῖα Νότου·

verses.18: Οὐκ ἐᾷ γάρ με ἀναπνεῦσαι· ἐνέπλησε δέ με πικρίας,

verses.20: Ἐὰν γὰρ ὦ δίκαιος, τὸ στόμα μου ἀσεβήσει· ἐάν τε ᾧ ἄμεμπτος, σκολιὸς ἀποβήσομαι.

verses.27: Ἐάν τε γὰρ εἶπω, ἐπιλήσομαι λαλῶν, συγκύψας τῷ προσώπῳ στενάξω·
verses.28: Σείομαι πᾶσι τοῖς μέλεσιν, οἴδα γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἀθῶόν με ἐάσεις.
verses.29: Ἐπειδὴ δέ εἰμι ἀσεβὴς, διὰ τί οὐκ ἀπέθανον;
verses.30: Ἐὰν γὰρ ἀπολούσωμαι χιόνι, καὶ ἀποκαθάρωμαι χερσὶ καθαραῖς,
verses.31: ἱκανῶς ἐν ῥύπῳ με ἔβαψας, ἐβδελύξατο δέ με ἡ στολή.
verses.32: Οὐ γὰρ εἰ ἄνθρωπος κατʼ ἐμὲ, ᾧ ἀντικρινοῦμαι, ἵνα ἔλθωμεν ὁμοθυμαδὸν εἰς κρίσιν.
verses.33: Εἴθε ἦν ὁ μεσίτης ἡμῶν, καὶ ἐλέγχων, καὶ διακούων ἀναμέσον ἀμφοτέρων.
verses.34: Ἀπαλλαξάτω ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ τὴν ῥάβδον, ὁ δὲ φόβος αὐτοῦ μή με στροβείτω,
verses.35: καὶ οὐ μὴ φοβηθῶ, ἀλλὰ λαλήσω· οὐ γὰρ οὕτω συνεπίσταμαι.

verses.1: Then Job answered and said,
verses.2: I know of a truth that it is so: for how shall a mortal man be just before the Lord?
verses.3: For if he would enter into judgment with him, God would not hearken to him, so that he should answer to one of his charges of a thousand.
verses.4: For he is wise in mind, and mighty, and great: who has hardened himself against him and endured?
verses.5: Who wears out the mountains, and men know it not: who overturns them in anger.
verses.6: Who shakes the earth under heaven from its foundations, and its pillars totter.
verses.7: Who commands the sun, and it rises not; and he seals up the stars.
verses.8: Who alone has stretched out the heavens, and walks on the sea as on firm ground.
verses.9: Who makes Pleias, and Hesperus, and Arcturus, and the chambers of the south.
verses.10: Who does great and unsearchable things; glorious also and excellent things, innumerable.
verses.11: If ever he should go beyond me, I shall not see him: if he should pass by me, neither thus have I known it.
verses.12: If he would take away, who shall turn him back? or who shall say to him, What hast thou done?
verses.13: For if he has turned away his anger, the whales under heaven have stooped under him.
verses.14: Oh then that he would hearken to me, or judge my cause.
verses.15: For though I be righteous, he will not hearken to me: I will intreat his judgment.
verses.16: And if I should call and he should not hearken, I cannot believe that he has listened to my voice.
verses.17: Let him not crush me with a dark storm: but he has made my bruises many without cause.
verses.18: For he suffers me not to take breath, but he has filled me with bitterness.
verses.19: For indeed he is strong in power: who then shall resist his judgment?
verses.20: For though I should seem righteous, my mouth will be profane: and though I should seem blameless, I shall be proved perverse.
verses.21: For even if I have sinned, I know it not in my soul: but my life is taken away.
verses.22: Wherefore I said, Wrath slays the great and mighty man.
verses.23: For the worthless die, but the righteous are laughed to scorn.
verses.24: For they are delivered into the hands of the unrighteous man: he covers the faces of the judges of the earth: but if it be not he, who is it?
verses.25: But my life is swifter than a post: my days have fled away, and they knew it not.
verses.26: Or again, is there a trace of their path left by ships? or is there one of the flying eagle as it seeks its prey?
verses.27: And if I should say, I will forget to speak, I will bow down my face and groan;
verses.28: I quake in all my limbs, for I know that thou wilt not leave me alone as innocent.
verses.29: But since I am ungodly, why have I not died?
verses.30: For if I should wash myself with snow, and purge myself with pure hands,
verses.31: thou hadst thoroughly plunged me in filth, and my garment had abhorred me.
verses.32: For thou art not man like me, with whom I could contend, that we might come together to judgment.
verses.33: Would that he our mediator were present, and a reprover, and one who should hear the cause between both.
verses.34: Let him remove his rod from me, and let not his fear terrify me:
verses.35: so shall I not be afraid, but I will speak: for I am not thus conscious of guilt.

verses.1: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.2: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.
verses.3: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
verses.4: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?
verses.5: Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man’s days,
verses.6: That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?
verses.7: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.
verses.8: Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.
verses.9: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?
verses.10: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
verses.11: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.
verses.12: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
verses.13: And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.
verses.14: If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.
verses.15: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;
verses.16: For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.
verses.17: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.
verses.18: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!
verses.19: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
verses.20: Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
verses.21: Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;
verses.22: A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.

verses.1: Καμνὼν τῇ ψυχῇ μου, στένων ἐπαφήσω ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰ ῥήματα μου· λαλήσω πικρίᾳ ψυχῆς μου συνεχόμενος,
verses.2: καὶ ἐρῶ πρὸς Κύριον, μή με ἀσεβεῖν δίδασκε· καὶ διατί με οὕτως ἔκρινας;

verses.4: Ἢ ὥσπερ βροτὸς ὁρᾷ, καθορᾷς; ἢ καθὼς ὁρᾷ ἄνθρωπος, βλέψῃ;
verses.5: Ἢ ὁ βίος σου ἀνθρώπινός ἐστιν, ἢ τὰ ἔτη σου ἀνδρὸς,

verses.14: Ἐάν τε γὰρ ἁμάρτω, φυλάσσεις με, ἀπὸ δὲ ἀνομίας οὐκ ἀθῶόν με πεποίηκας.

verses.16: Ἀγρεύομαι γὰρ ὥσπερ λέων εἰς σφαγήν· πάλιν γὰρ μεταβαλὼν δεινῶς με ὀλέκεις,
verses.17: ἐπανακαινίζων ἐπʼ ἐμὲ τὴν ἔτασίν μου· ὀργῇ δὲ μεγάλῃ μοι ἐχρήσω, ἐπήγαγες δὲ ἐπʼ ἐμὲ πειρατήρια.
verses.18: Ἱνατί οὖν ἐκ κοιλίας με ἐξήγαγες, καὶ οὐκ ἀπέθανον, ὀφθαλμὸς δέ με οὐκ εἶδε,

verses.20: Ἢ οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐστὶν ὁ βίος τοῦ χρόνου μου; ἔασόν με ἀναπαύσασθαι μικρὸν,
verses.21: πρὸ τοῦ με πορευθῆναι ὅθεν οὐκ ἀναστρέψω, εἰς γῆν σκοτεινὴν καὶ γνοφερὰν,
verses.22: εἰς γῆν σκότους αἰωνίου, οὗ οὐκ ἔστι φέγγος, οὐδὲ ὁρᾷν ζωὴν βροτῶν.

verses.1: Weary in my soul, I will pour my words with groans upon him: I will speak being straitened in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.2: And I will say to the Lord, Do not teach me to be impious; and wherefore hast thou thus judged me?
verses.3: Is it good before thee if I be unrighteous? for thou hast disowned the work of thy hands, and attended to the counsel of the ungodly.
verses.4: Or dost thou see as a mortal sees? or wilt thou look as a man sees?
verses.5: Or is thy life human, or thy years the years of a man,
verses.6: that thou hast enquired into mine iniquity, and searched out my sins?
verses.7: For thou knowest that I have not committed iniquity: but who is he that can deliver out of thy hands?
verses.8: Thy hands have formed me and made me; afterwards thou didst change thy mind, and smite me.
verses.9: Remember that thou hast made me as clay, and thou dost turn me again to earth.
verses.10: Hast thou not poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?
verses.11: And thou didst clothe me with skin and flesh, and frame me with bones and sinews.
verses.12: And thou didst bestow upon me life and mercy, and thy oversight has preserved my spirit.
verses.13: Having these things in thyself, I know that thou canst do all things; for nothing is impossible with thee.
verses.14: And if I should sin, thou watchest me; and thou hast not cleared me from iniquity.
verses.15: Or if I should be ungodly, woe is me: and if I should be righteous, I cannot lift myself up, for I am full of dishonour.
verses.16: For I am hunted like a lion for slaughter; for again thou hast changed and art terribly destroying me;
verses.17: renewing against me my torture: and thou hast dealt with me in great anger, and thou hast brought trials upon me.
verses.18: Why then didst thou bring me out of the womb? and why did I not die, and no eye see me,
verses.19: and I become as if I had not been? for why was I not carried from the womb to the grave?
verses.20: Is not the time of my life short? suffer me to rest a little,
verses.21: before I go whence I shall not return, to a land of darkness and gloominess;
verses.22: to a land of perpetual darkness, where there is no light, neither can any one see the life of mortals.

verses.1: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
verses.2: Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified?
verses.3: Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?
verses.4: For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.
verses.5: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;
verses.6: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.
verses.7: Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?
verses.8: It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?
verses.9: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
verses.10: If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?
verses.11: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it?
verses.12: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass’s colt.
verses.13: If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;
verses.14: If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.
verses.15: For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:
verses.16: Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away:
verses.17: And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday; thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.
verses.18: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.
verses.19: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.
verses.20: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost.

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Σωφὰρ ὁ Μιναῖος, λέγει,

verses.3: εὐλογημένος γεννητὸς γυναικὸς ὀλιγόβιος. Μὴ πολὺς ἐν ῥήμασι γίνου, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἀντικρινόμενός σοι;

verses.7: Ἢ ἴχνος Κυρίου εὑρήσεις, ἢ εἰς τὰ ἔσχατα ἀφίκου ἃ ἐποίησεν ὁ παντοκράτωρ;
verses.8: Ὑψηλὸς ὁ οὐρανὸς, καὶ τί ποιήσεις; βαθύτερα δὲ τῶν ἐν ᾅδου, τί οἶδας;
verses.9: ἢ μακρότερα μέτρου γῆς, ἢ εὔρους θαλάσσης;

verses.13: Εἰ γὰρ σὺ καθαρὰν ἔθου τὴν καρδίαν σου, ὑπτιάζεις δὲ χεῖρας πρὸς αὐτὸν,
verses.14: εἰ ἄνομόν τί ἐστιν ἐν χερσί σου, πόῤῥω ποίησον αὐτὸ ἀπὸ σοῦ, ἀδικία δὲ ἐν διαίτῃ σου μὴ αὐλισθήτω·
verses.15: Οὕτως γὰρ ἀναλάμψει σου τὸ πρόσωπον, ὥσπερ ὕδωρ καθαρὸν, ἐκδύσῃ δὲ ῥύπον, καὶ οὐ μὴ φοβηθήσῃ·
verses.16: Καὶ τὸν κόπον ἐπιλήσῃ, ὥσπερ κῦμα παρελθὸν, καὶ οὐ πτοηθήσῃ·

verses.18: Πεποιθώς τε ἔσῃ, ὅτι ἐστί σοι ἐλπὶς, ἐκ δὲ μερίμνης καὶ φροντίδος ἀναφανεῖταί σοι εἰρήνη·
verses.19: Ἡσυχάσεις γὰρ, καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ πολεμῶν σε· μεταβαλόμενοι δὲ πολλοί σου δεηθήσονται.
verses.20: Σωτηρία δὲ αὐτοὺς ἀπολείψει· ἡ γὰρ ἐλπὶς αὐτῶν ἀπώλεια, ὀφθαλμοὶ δὲ ἀσεβῶν τακήσονται.

verses.1: Then Sophar the Minæan answered and said,
verses.2: He that speaks much, should also hear on the other side: or does the fluent speaker think himself to be righteous? blessed is the short-lived offspring of woman.
verses.3: Be not a speaker of many words; for is there none to answer thee?
verses.4: For say not, I am pure in my works, and blameless before him.
verses.5: But oh that the Lord would speak to thee, and open his lips with thee!
verses.6: Then shall he declare to thee the power of wisdom; for it shall be double of that which is with thee: and then shalt thou know, that a just recompence of thy sins has come to thee from the Lord.
verses.7: Wilt thou find out the traces of the Lord? or hast thou come to the end of that which the Almighty has made?
verses.8: Heaven is high; and what wilt thou do? and there are deeper things than those in hell; what dost thou know?
verses.9: Or longer than the measure of the earth, or the breadth of the sea.
verses.10: And if he should overthrow all things, who will say to him, What hast thou done?
verses.11: For he knows the works of transgressors; and when he sees wickedness, he will not overlook it.
verses.12: But man vainly buoys himself up with words; and a mortal born of woman is like an ass of the desert.
verses.13: For if thou hast made thine heart pure, and liftest up thine hands towards him;
verses.14: if there is any iniquity in thy hands, put it far from thee, and let not unrighteousness lodge in thy habitation.
verses.15: For thus shall thy countenance shine again, as pure water; and thou shalt divest thyself of uncleanness, and shalt not fear.
verses.16: And thou shalt forget trouble, as a wave that has passed by; and thou shalt not be scared.
verses.17: And thy prayer shall be as the morning star, and life shall arise to thee as from the noon-day.
verses.18: And thou shalt be confident, because thou hast hope; and peace shall dawn to thee from out of anxiety and care.
verses.19: For thou shalt be at ease, and there shall be no one to fight against thee; and many shall charge, and make supplication to thee.
verses.20: But safety shall fail them; for their hope is destruction, and the eyes of the ungodly shall waste away.

verses.1: And Job answered and said,
verses.2: No doubt but ye are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
verses.3: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?
verses.4: I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn.
verses.5: He that is ready to slip with his feet is as a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.
verses.6: The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.
verses.7: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee:
verses.8: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.
verses.9: Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the LORD hath wrought this?
verses.10: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.
verses.11: Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat?
verses.12: With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.
verses.13: With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.
verses.14: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.
verses.15: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.
verses.16: With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.
verses.17: He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools.
verses.18: He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.
verses.19: He leadeth princes away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty.
verses.20: He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.
verses.21: He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty.
verses.22: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death.
verses.23: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.
verses.24: He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
verses.25: They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἰὼβ, λέγει,

verses.1: And Job answered and said,
verses.2: So then ye alone are men, and wisdom shall die with you?
verses.3: But I also have a heart as well as you.
verses.4: For a righteous and blameless man has become a subject for mockery.
verses.5: For it had been ordained that he should fall under others at the appointed time, and that his houses should be spoiled by transgressors: let not however any one trust that, being evil, he shall be held guiltless,
verses.6: even as many as provoke the Lord, as if there were indeed to be no inquisition made of them.
verses.7: But ask now the beasts, if they may speak to thee; and the birds of the air, if they may declare to thee.
verses.8: Tell the earth, if it may speak to thee: and the fishes of the sea shall explain to thee.
verses.9: Who then has not known in all these things, that the hand of the Lord has made them?
verses.10: Whereas the life of all living things is in his hand, and the breath of every man.
verses.11: For the ear tries words, and the palate tastes meats.
verses.12: In length of time is wisdom, and in long life knowledge.
verses.13: With him are wisdom and power, with him counsel and understanding.
verses.14: If he should cast down, who will build up? if he should shut up against men, who shall open?
verses.15: If he should withhold the water, he will dry the earth: and if he should let it loose, he overthrows and destroys it.
verses.16: With him are strength and power: he has knowledge and understanding.
verses.17: He leads counsellors away captive, and maddens the judges of the earth.
verses.18: He seats kings upon thrones, and girds their loins with a girdle.
verses.19: He sends away priests into captivity, and overthrows the mighty ones of the earth.
verses.20: He changes the lips of the trusty, and he knows the understanding of the elders.
verses.21: He pours dishonour upon princes, and heals the lowly.
verses.22: Revealing deep things out of darkness: and he has brought into light the shadow of death.
verses.23: Causing the nations to wander, and destroying them: overthrowing the nations, and leading them away.
verses.24: Perplexing the minds of the princes of the earth: and he causes them to wander in a way they have not known, saying,
verses.25: Let them grope in darkness, and let there be no light, and let them wander as a drunken man.

verses.1: Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.
verses.2: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.
verses.3: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such an one, and bringest me into judgment with thee?
verses.4: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
verses.5: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;
verses.6: Turn from him, that he may rest, till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day.
verses.7: For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.
verses.8: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground;
verses.9: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.
verses.10: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?
verses.11: As the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up:
verses.12: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.
verses.13: O that thou wouldest hide me in the grave, that thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!
verses.14: If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.
verses.15: Thou shalt call, and I will answer thee: thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands.
verses.16: For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin?
verses.17: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity.
verses.18: And surely the mountain falling cometh to nought, and the rock is removed out of his place.
verses.19: The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow out of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man.
verses.20: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth: thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.
verses.21: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.
verses.22: But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn.

verses.1: Βρότος γὰρ γεννητὸς γυναικὸς, ὀλιγόβιος, καὶ πλήρης ὀργῆς·
verses.2: ἢ ὥσπερ ἄνθος ἀνθῆσαν ἐξέπεσεν, ἀπέδρα δὲ ὥσπερ σκιὰ, καὶ οὐ μὴ στῇ.
verses.3: Οὐχὶ καὶ τούτου λόγον ἐποιήσω, καὶ τοῦτον ἐποίησας εἰσελθεῖν ἐν κρίματι ἐνώπιόν σου;
verses.4: Τίς γὰρ καθαρὸς ἔσται ἀπὸ ῥύπου; ἀλλʼ οὐθεὶς,
verses.5: ἐὰν καὶ μία ἡμέρα ὁ βίος αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· ἀριθμητοὶ δὲ μῆνες αὐτοῦ παρʼ αὐτοῦ· εἰς χρόνον ἔθου, καὶ οὐ μὴ ὑπερβῇ.
verses.6: Ἀπόστα ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἡσυχάσῃ, καὶ εὐδοκήσῃ τὸν βίον, ὥσπερ ὁ μισθωτός.
verses.7: Ἔστι γὰρ δένδρῳ ἐλπὶς, ἐὰν γὰρ ἐκκοπῇ, ἔτι ἐπανθήσει, καὶ ὁ ῥάδαμνος αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ ἐκλείπῃ.

verses.10: Ἀνὴρ δὲ τελευτήσας ᾤχετο, πεσὼν δὲ βροτὸς οὐκ ἔτι ἐστί.

verses.12: Ἄνθρωπος δὲ κοιμηθεὶς οὐ μὴν ἀναστῇ ἕως ἂν ὁ οὐρανὸς οὐ μὴ συῤῥαφῇ, καὶ οὐκ ἐξυπνισθήσονται ἐξ ὕπνου αὐτῶν.
verses.13: Εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον ἐν ᾅδῃ με ἐφύλαξας, ἔκρυψας δέ με ἕως ἂν παύσηταί σου ἡ ὀργὴ, καὶ τάξῃ μοι χρόνον ἐν ᾧ μνείαν μου ποιήσῃ.
verses.14: Ἐὰν γὰρ ἀποθάνῃ ἄνθρωπος, ζήσεται συντελέσας ἡμέρας τοῦ βίου αὐτοῦ· ὑπομενῶ ἕως πάλιν γένωμαι;
verses.15: Εἶτα καλέσεις, ἐγὼ δέ σοι ὑπακούσομαι, τὰ δὲ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν σου μὴ ἀποποιοῦ.
verses.16: Ἠρίθμησας δέ μου τὰ ἐπιτηδεύματα, καὶ οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ σε οὐδὲν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν μου;
verses.17: Ἐσφράγισας δέ μου τὰς ἀνομίας ἐν βαλαντίῳ, ἐπεσημῄνω δὲ εἴτι ἄκων παρέβην.
verses.18: Καὶ πλὴν ὄρος πίπτον διαπεσεῖται, καὶ πέτρα παλαιωθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτῆς.
verses.19: Λίθους ἐλέαναν ὕδατα, καὶ κατέκλυσεν ὕδατα ὕπτια τοῦ χώματος τῆς γῆς· καὶ ὑπομονὴν ἀνθρώπου ἀπώλεσας.
verses.20: Ὦσας αὐτὸν εἰς τέλος, καὶ ᾤχετο· ἐπέστησας αὐτῷ τὸ πρόσωπον, καὶ ἐξαπέστειλας,
verses.21: πολλὼν δὲ γενομένων τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ, οὐκ οἶδεν· ἐὰν δὲ ὀλίγοι γένωνται, οὐκ ἐπέσταται.
verses.22: Ἀλλʼ ἢ αἱ σάρκες αὐτοῦ ἤλγησαν, ἡ δὲ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπένθησεν.

verses.1: For a mortal born of a woman is short-lived, and full of wrath.
verses.2: Or he falls like a flower that has bloomed; and he departs like a shadow, and cannot continue.
verses.3: Hast thou not taken account even of him, and caused him to enter into judgment before thee?
verses.4: For who shall be pure from uncleanness? not even one;
verses.5: if even his life should be but one day upon the earth: and his months are numbered by him: thou hast appointed him for a time, and he shall by no means exceed it.
verses.6: Depart from him, that he may be quiet, and take pleasure in his life, though as a hireling.
verses.7: For there is hope for a tree, even if it should be cut down, that it shall blossom again, and its branch shall not fail.
verses.8: For though its root should grow old in the earth, and its stem die in the rock;
verses.9: it will blossom from the scent of water, and will produce a crop, as one newly planted.
verses.10: But a man that has died is utterly gone; and when a mortal has fallen, he is no more.
verses.11: For the sea wastes in length of time, and a river fails and is dried up.
verses.12: And man that has lain down in death shall certainly not rise again till the heaven be dissolved, and they shall not awake from their sleep.
verses.13: For oh that thou hadst kept me in the grave, and hadst hidden me until thy wrath should cease, and thou shouldest set me a time in which thou wouldest remember me!
verses.14: For if a man should die, shall he live again, having accomplished the days of his life? I will wait till I exist again?
verses.15: Then shalt thou call, and I will hearken to thee: but do not thou reject the work of thine hands.
verses.16: But thou hast numbered my devices: and not one of my sins shall escape thee?
verses.17: And thou hast sealed up my transgressions in a bag, and marked if I have been guilty of any transgression unawares.
verses.18: And verily a mountain falling will utterly be destroyed, and a rock shall be worn out of its place.
verses.19: The waters wear the stones, and waters falling headlong overflow a heap of the earth: and thou destroyest the hope of man.
verses.20: Thou drivest him to an end, and he is gone: thou settest thy face against him, and sendest him away;
verses.21: and though his children be multiplied, he knows it not; and if they be few, he is not aware.
verses.22: But his flesh is in pain, and his soul mourns.

verses.1: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
verses.2: Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?
verses.3: Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?
verses.4: Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God.
verses.5: For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.
verses.6: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee.
verses.7: Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills?
verses.8: Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?
verses.9: What knowest thou, that we know not? what understandest thou, which is not in us?
verses.10: With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.
verses.11: Are the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?
verses.12: Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at,
verses.13: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth?
verses.14: What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
verses.15: Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight.
verses.16: How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?
verses.17: I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare;
verses.18: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid it:
verses.19: Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.
verses.20: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.
verses.21: A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.
verses.22: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.
verses.23: He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
verses.24: Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
verses.25: For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty.
verses.26: He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:
verses.27: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks.
verses.28: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.
verses.29: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth.
verses.30: He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away.
verses.31: Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence.
verses.32: It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green.
verses.33: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive.
verses.34: For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.
verses.35: They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.

verses.19: Αὐτοῖς μόνοις ἐδόθη ἡ γῆ, καὶ οὐκ ἐπῆλθεν ἀλλογενὴς ἐπʼ αὐτούς.

verses.28: Αὐλισθείη δὲ πόλεις ἐρήμους, εἰσέλθοι δὲ εἰς οἴκους ἀοικήτους· ἃ δὲ ἐκεῖνοι ἡτοίμασαν, ἄλλοι ἀποίσονται.
verses.29: Οὔτε μὴ πλουτισθῇ, οὔτε μὴ μείνῃ αὐτοῦ τὰ ὑπάρχοντα· οὐ μὴ βάλῃ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν σκιὰν,

verses.31: Μὴ πιστευέτω ὅτι ὑπομενεῖ, κενὰ γὰρ ἀποβήσεται αὐτῷ.
verses.32: Ἡ τομὴ αὐτοῦ πρὸ ὥρας φθαρήσεται, καὶ ὁ ῥάδαμνος αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ πυκάσῃ.
verses.33: Τρυγηθείη δὲ ὡς ὄμφαξ πρὸ ὥρας, ἐκπέσοι δὲ ὡς ἄνθος ἐλαίας.
verses.34: Μαρτύριον γὰρ ἀσεβοῦς θάνατος· πῦρ δὲ καύσει οἴκους δωροδεκτῶν·
verses.35: Ἐν γαστρὶ δὲ λήψεται ὀδύνας, ἀποβήσεται δὲ αὐτῷ κενὰ, ἡ δὲ κοιλία αὐτοῦ ὑποίσει δόλον.

verses.1: Then Eliphaz the Thæmanite answered and said,
verses.2: Will a wise man give for answer a mere breath of wisdom? and does he fill up the pain of his belly,
verses.3: reasoning with improper sayings, and with words wherein is no profit?
verses.4: Hast not thou moreover cast off fear, and accomplished such words before the Lord?
verses.5: Thou art guilty by the words of thy mouth, neither hast thou discerned the words of the mighty.
verses.6: Let thine own mouth, and not me, reprove thee: and thy lips shall testify against thee.
verses.7: What! art thou the first man that was born? or wert thou established before the hills?
verses.8: Or hast thou heard the ordinance of the Lord? or has God used thee as his counsellor? and has wisdom come only to thee?
verses.9: For what knowest thou, that we know not? or what understandest thou, which we do not also?
verses.10: Truly among us are both the old and very aged man, more advanced in days than thy father.
verses.11: Thou hast been scourged for but few of thy sins: thou hast spoken haughtily and extravagantly.
verses.12: What has thine heart dared? or what have thine eyes aimed at,
verses.13: that thou hast vented thy rage before the Lord, and delivered such words from thy mouth?
verses.14: For who, being a mortal, is such that he shall be blameless? or, who that is born of a woman, that he should be just?
verses.15: Forasmuch as he trusts not his saints; and the heaven is not pure before him.
verses.16: Alas then, abominable and unclean is man, drinking unrighteousness as a draught.
verses.17: But I will tell thee, hearken to me; I will tell thee now what I have seen;
verses.18: things wise men say, and their fathers have not hidden.
verses.19: To them alone the earth was given, and no stranger came upon them.
verses.20: All the life of the ungodly is spent in care, and the years granted to the oppressor are numbered.
verses.21: And his terror is in his ears: just when he seems to be at peace, his overthrow will come.
verses.22: Let him not trust that he shall return from darkness, for he has been already made over to the power of the sword.
verses.23: And he has been appointed to be food for vultures; and he knows within himself that he is doomed to be a carcase: and a dark day shall carry him away as with a whirlwind.
verses.24: Distress also and anguish shall come upon him: he shall fall as a captain in the first rank.
verses.25: For he has lifted his hands against the Lord, and he has hardened his neck against the Almighty Lord.
verses.26: And he has run against him with insolence, on the thickness of the back of his shield.
verses.27: For he has covered his face with his fat, and made layers of fat upon his thighs.
verses.28: And let him lodge in desolate cities, and enter into houses without inhabitant: and what they have prepared, others shall carry away.
verses.29: Neither shall he at all grow rich, nor shall his substance remain: he shall not cast a shadow upon the earth.
verses.30: Neither shall he in any wise escape the darkness: let the wind blast his blossom, and let his flower fall off.
verses.31: Let him not think that he shall endure; for his end shall be vanity.
verses.32: His harvest shall perish before the time, and his branch shall not flourish.
verses.33: And let him be gathered as the unripe grape before the time, and let him fall as the blossom of the olive.
verses.34: For death is the witness of an ungodly man, and fire shall burn the houses of them that receive gifts.
verses.35: And he shall conceive sorrows, and his end shall be vanity, and his belly shall bear deceit.

verses.1: Then Job answered and said,

verses.4: Μὴ ταῦτα ἔγνως ἀπὸ τοῦ ἔτι, ἀφʼ οὗ ἐτέθη ἄνθρωπος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
verses.5: Εὐφροσύνη δὲ ἀσεβῶν πτῶμα ἐξαίσιον, χαρμονὴ δὲ παρανόμων ἀπώλεια·
verses.6: ἐὰν ἀναβῇ εἰς οὐρανὸν αὐτοῦ τὰ δῶρα, ἡ δὲ θυσία αὐτοῦ νεφῶν ἅψηται.
verses.7: Ὅταν γὰρ δοκῇ ἤδη κατεστηρίχθαι, τότε εἰς τέλος ἀπολεῖται· οἱ δὲ εἰδότες αὐτὸν ἐροῦσι, ποῦ ἐστιν;
verses.8: Ὥσπερ ἐνύπνιον ἐκπετασθὲν οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ, ἔπτη δὲ ὥσπερ φάσμα νυκτερινόν.
verses.9: Ὀφθαλμὸς παρέβλεψε, καὶ οὐ προσθήσει, καὶ οὐκ ἔτι προσνοήσει αὐτὸν ὁ τόπος αὐτοῦ.
verses.10: Τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ὀλέσαισαν ἥττονες, αἱ δὲ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ πυρσεύσαισαν ὀδύνας.
verses.11: Ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ ἐνεπλήσθησαν νεότητος αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ χώματος κοιμηθήσεται.
verses.12: Ἐὰν γλυκανθῇ ἐν στόματι αὐτοῦ κακία, κρύψει αὐτὴν ὑπὸ τὴν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ,
verses.13: οὐ φείσεται αὐτῆς, καὶ οὐκ ἐγκαταλείψει αὐτήν· καὶ συνάξει αὐτὴν ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ λάρυγγος αὐτοῦ,
verses.14: καὶ οὐ μὴ δυνηθῇ βοηθῆσαι ἑαυτῷ· χολὴ ἀσπίδος ἐν γαστρὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.15: Πλοῦτος ἀδίκως συναγόμενος ἐξεμεθήσεται, ἐξ οἰκίας αὐτοῦ ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἄγγελος.
verses.16: Θυμὸν δὲ δρακόντων θηλάσειεν, ἀνέλοι δὲ αὐτὸν γλῶσσα ὄφεως.
verses.17: Μὴ ἴδοι ἄμελξιν νομάδων, μηδὲ νομὰς μέλιτος καὶ βουτύρου.
verses.18: Εἰς κενὰ καὶ μάταια ἐκοπίασε, πλοῦτον ἐξ οὗ οὐ γεύσεται· ὥσπερ στρίφνος ἀμάσητος, ἀκατάποτος.
verses.19: Πολλῶν γὰρ δυνατῶν οἴκους ἔθλασε· δίαιταν δὲ ἥρπασε, καὶ οὐκ ἔστησεν.
verses.20: Οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ σωτηρία τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν, ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ αὐτοῦ οὐ σωθήσεται.
verses.21: Οὐκ ἔστιν ὑπόλειμμα τοῖς βρώμασιν αὐτοῦ, διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀνθήσει αὐτοῦ τὰ ἀγαθά.
verses.22: Ὅταν δὲ δοκῇ ἤδη πεπληρῶσθαι, θλιβήσεται, πᾶσα δὲ ἀνάγκη ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἐπελεύσεται.
verses.23: Εἴ πῶς εἶ πληρῶσαι γαστέρα αὐτοῦ, ἐπαποστείλαι ἐπʼ αὐτὸν θυμὸν ὀργῆς, νίψαι ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ὀδύνας,
verses.24: καὶ οὐ μὴ σωθῇ ἐκ χειρὸς σιδήρου· τρώσαι αὐτὸν τόξον χάλκειον.
verses.25: Διεξέλθοι δὲ διὰ σώματος αὐτοῦ βέλος, ἄστρα δὲ ἐν διαίταις αὐτοῦ· περιπατήσαισαν ἐπʼ αὐτῷ φόβοι,
verses.26: πᾶν δὲ σκότος αὐτῷ ὑπομείναι· κατέδεται αὐτὸν πῦρ ἄκαυστον, κακώσαι δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπήλυτος τὸν οἶκον.
verses.27: Ἀνακάλυψαι δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ οὐρανὸς τὰς ἀνομίας, γῆ δὲ ἐπανασταίη αὐτῷ.
verses.28: Ἑλκύσαι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεια εἰς τέλος, ἡμέρα ὀργῆς ἐπέλθοι αὐτῷ.
verses.29: Αὕτη ἡ μέρις ἀνθρώπου ἀσεβοῦς παρὰ Κυρίου, καὶ κτῆμα ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ παρὰ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου.

verses.1: Then Sophar the Minæan answered and said,
verses.2: I did not suppose that thou wouldest answer thus: neither do ye understand more than I.
verses.3: I will hear my shameful reproach; and the spirit of my understanding answers me.
verses.4: Hast thou not known these things of old, from the time that man was set upon the earth?
verses.5: But the mirth of the ungodly is a signal downfall, and the joy of transgressors is destruction:
verses.6: although his gifts should go up to heaven, and his sacrifice reach the clouds.
verses.7: For when he shall seem to be now established, then he shall utterly perish: and they that knew him shall say, Where is he?
verses.8: Like a dream that has fled away, he shall not be found; and he has fled like a vision of the night.
verses.9: The eye has looked upon him, but shall not see him again; and his place shall no longer perceive him.
verses.10: Let his inferiors destroy his children, and let his hands kindle the fire of sorrow.
verses.11: His bones have been filled with vigour of his youth, and it shall lie down with him in the dust.
verses.12: Though evil be sweet in his mouth, though he will hide it under his tongue;
verses.13: though he will not spare it, and will not leave it, but will keep it in the midst of his throat:
verses.14: yet he shall not at all be able to help himself; the gall of an asp is in his belly.
verses.15: His wealth unjustly collected shall be vomited up; a messenger of wrath shall drag him out of his house.
verses.16: And let him suck the poison of serpents, and let the serpent's tongue slay him.
verses.17: Let him not see the milk of the pastures, nor the supplies of honey and butter.
verses.18: He has laboured unprofitably and in vain, for wealth of which he shall not taste: it is as a lean thing, unfit for food, which he cannot swallow.
verses.19: For he has broken down the houses of many mighty men: and he has plundered an habitation, though he built it not.
verses.20: There is no security to his possessions; he shall not be saved by his desire.
verses.21: There is nothing remaining of his provisions; therefore his goods shall not flourish.
verses.22: But when he shall seem to be just satisfied, he shall be straitened; and all distress shall come upon him.
verses.23: If by any means he would fill his belly, let God send upon him the fury of wrath; let him bring a torrent of pains upon him.
verses.24: And he shall by no means escape from the power of the sword; let the brazen bow wound him.
verses.25: And let the arrow pierce through his body; and let the stars be against his dwelling-place: let terrors come upon him.
verses.26: And let all darkness wait for him: a fire that burns not out shall consume him; and let a stranger plague his house.
verses.27: And let the heaven reveal his iniquities, and the earth rise up against him.
verses.28: Let destruction bring his house to an end; let a day of wrath come upon him.
verses.29: This is the portion of an ungodly man from the Lord, and the possession of his goods appointed him by the all-seeing God.

verses.1: But Job answered and said,
verses.2: Hear diligently my speech, and let this be your consolations.
verses.3: Suffer me that I may speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on.
verses.4: As for me, is my complaint to man? and if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled?
verses.5: Mark me, and be astonished, and lay your hand upon your mouth.
verses.6: Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh.
verses.7: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?
verses.8: Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes.
verses.9: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.
verses.10: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.
verses.11: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.
verses.12: They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.
verses.13: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.
verses.14: Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.
verses.15: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?
verses.16: Lo, their good is not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
verses.17: How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and how oft cometh their destruction upon them! God distributeth sorrows in his anger.
verses.18: They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.
verses.19: God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know it.
verses.20: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
verses.21: For what pleasure hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?
verses.22: Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.
verses.23: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.
verses.24: His breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.
verses.25: And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure.
verses.26: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them.
verses.27: Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices which ye wrongfully imagine against me.
verses.28: For ye say, Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?
verses.29: Have ye not asked them that go by the way? and do ye not know their tokens,
verses.30: That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.
verses.31: Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him what he hath done?
verses.32: Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb.
verses.33: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as there are innumerable before him.
verses.34: How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood?

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἰὼβ, λέγει,
verses.2: Ἀκούσατε ἀκούσατέ μου τῶν λόγων, ἵνα μὴ ᾖ μοι παρʼ ὑμῶν αὕτη ἡ παράκλησις.
verses.3: Ἄρατέ με, ἐγὼ δὲ λαλήσω, εἶτʼ οὐ καταγελάσετέ μου.
verses.4: Τί γάρ; μὴ ἀνθρώπου μου ἡ ἔλεγξις; ἢ διὰ τί οὐ θυμωθήσομαι;
verses.5: Εἰσβλέψαντες εἰς ἐμὲ θαυμάσετε, χεῖρα θέντες ἐπὶ σιαγόνι.
verses.6: Ἐάν τε γὰρ μνησθῶ, ἐσπούδακα· ἔχουσι δέ μου τὰς σάρκας ὀδύναι.
verses.7: Διὰ τί ἀσεβεῖς ζῶσι, πεπαλαίωνται δὲ καὶ ἐν πλούτῳ;
verses.8: Ὁ σπόρος αὐτῶν κατὰ ψυχὴν, τὰ δὲ τέκνα αὐτῶν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς.
verses.9: Οἱ οἶκοι αὐτῶν εὐθηνοῦσι, φόβος δὲ οὐδαμοῦ, μάστιξ δὲ παρὰ Κυρίου οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς.
verses.10: Ἡ βοῦς αὐτῶν οὐκ ὠμοτόκησε, διεσώθη δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα καὶ οὐκ ἔσφαλε.
verses.11: Μένουσι δὲ ὡς πρόβατα αἰώνια, τὰ δὲ παιδία αὐτῶν προσπαίζουσιν,
verses.12: ἀναλαβόντες ψαλτήριον καὶ κιθάραν, καὶ εὐφραίνονται φωνῇ ψαλμοῦ.
verses.13: Συνετέλεσαν δὲ ἐν ἀγαθοῖς τὸν βίον αὐτῶν, ἐν δὲ ἀναπαύσει ᾅδου ἐκοιμήθησαν.
verses.14: Λέγει δὲ Κυρίῳ, ἀπόστα ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, ὁδούς σου εἰδέναι οὐ βούλομαι.
verses.15: Τί ἱκανὸς, ὅτι δουλεύσομεν αὐτῷ; καὶ τίς ὠφέλεια, ὅτι ἀπαντήσομεν αὐτῷ;
verses.16: Ἐν χερσὶ γὰρ ἦν αὐτῶν τὰ ἀγαθὰ, ἔργα δὲ ἀσεβῶν οὐκ ἐφορᾷ.
verses.17: Οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀσεβῶν λύχνος σβεσθήσεται, ἐπελεύσεται δὲ αὐτοῖς ἡ καταστροφὴ, ὠδῖνες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἕξουσιν ἀπὸ ὀργῆς.
verses.18: Ἔσονται δὲ ὥσπερ ἄχυρα ὑπʼ ἀνέμου, ἢ ὥσπερ κονιορτὸς ὃν ὑφείλετο λαίλαψ.
verses.19: Ἐκλείποι υἱοὺς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ, ἀνταποδώσει πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ γνώσεται.
verses.20: Ἴδοισαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ σφαγὴν, ἀπὸ δὲ Κυρίου μὴ διασωθείη.
verses.21: Ὅτι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ἐν οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀριθμοὶ μηνῶν αὐτοῦ διῃρέθησαν.
verses.22: Πότερον οὐχὶ ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν ὁ διδάσκων σύνεσιν καὶ ἐπιστήμην; αὐτὸς δὲ φόνους διακρίνει;
verses.23: Οὗτος ἀποθανεῖται ἐν κράτει ἁπλοσύνης αὐτοῦ, ὅλος δὲ εὐπαθῶν καὶ εὐθηνῶν.
verses.24: Τὰ δὲ ἔγκατα αὐτοὺ πλήρη στέατος, μυελὸς δὲ αὐτοῦ διαχεῖται.
verses.25: Ὁ δὲ τελευτᾷ ὑπὸ πικρίας ψυχῆς, οὐ φαγὼν οὐδὲν ἀγαθόν.
verses.26: Ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ ἐπὶ γῆς κοιμῶνται, σαπρία δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐκάλυψεν.
verses.27: Ὥστε οἶδα ὑμᾶς, ὅτι τόλμῃ ἐπίκεισθέ μοι·
verses.28: Ὥστε ἐρεῖτε, ποῦ ἐστιν οἶκος ἄρχοντος; καὶ ποῦ ἐστιν ἡ σκέπη τῶν σκηνωμάτων τῶν ἀσεβῶν;
verses.29: Ἐρωτήσατε παραπορευομένους ὁδὸν, καὶ τὰ σημεῖα αὐτῶν οὐκ ἀπαλλοτριώσετε.
verses.30: Ὅτι εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπωλείας κουφίζεται ὁ πονηρὸς, εἰς ἡμέραν ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ ἀπαχθήσονται.
verses.31: Τίς ἀπαγγελεῖ ἐπὶ προσώπου αὐτοῦ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐποίησε; τίς ἀνταποδώσει αὐτῷ;
verses.32: Καὶ αὐτὸς εἰς τάφους ἀπηνέχθη, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπὶ σωρῶν ἠγρύπνησεν.
verses.33: Ἐγλυκάνθησαν αὐτῷ χάλικες χειμάῤῥου, καὶ ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ἀπελεύσεται, καὶ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ἀναρίθμητοι.
verses.34: Πῶς δὲ παρακαλεῖτέ με κενά; τὸ δὲ ἐμὲ καταπαύσασθαι ἀφʼ ὑμῶν οὐδέν.
