verses.1: But Job answered and said,
verses.2: Hear ye, hear ye my words, that I may not have this consolation from you.
verses.3: Raise me, and I will speak; then ye shall not laugh me to scorn.
verses.4: What! is my reproof of man? and why should I not be angry?
verses.5: Look upon me, and wonder, laying your hand upon your cheek.
verses.6: For even when I remember, I am alarmed, and pains seize my flesh.
verses.7: Wherefore do the ungodly live, and grow old even in wealth?
verses.8: Their seed is according to their desire, and their children are in their sight.
verses.9: Their houses are prosperous, neither have they any where cause for fear, neither is there a scourge from the Lord upon them.
verses.10: Their cow does not cast her calf, and their beast with young is safe, and does not miscarry.
verses.11: And they remain as an unfailing flock, and their children play before them, taking up the psaltery and harp;
verses.12: and they rejoice at the voice of a song.
verses.13: And they spend their days in wealth, and fall asleep in the rest of the grave.
verses.14: Yet such a man says to the Lord, Depart from me; I desire not to know thy ways.
verses.15: What is the Mighty One, that we should serve him? and what profit is there that we should approach him?
verses.16: For their good things were in their hands, but he regards not the works of the ungodly.
verses.17: Nevertheless, the lamp of the ungodly also shall be put out, and destruction shall come upon them, and pangs of vengeance shall seize them.
verses.18: And they shall be as chaff before the wind, or as dust which the storm has taken up.
verses.19: Let his substance fail to supply his children: God shall recompense him, and he shall know it.
verses.20: Let his eyes see his own destruction, and let him not be saved by the Lord.
verses.21: For his desire is in his house with him, and the number of his months has been suddenly cut off.
verses.22: Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge? and does not he judge murders?
verses.23: One shall die in his perfect strength, and wholly at ease and prosperous;
verses.24: and his inwards are full of fat, and his marrow is diffused throughout him.
verses.25: And another dies in bitterness of soul, not eating any good thing.
verses.26: But they lie down in the earth together, and corruption covers them.
verses.27: So I know you, that ye presumptuously attack me:
verses.28: so that ye will say, Where is the house of the prince? and where is the covering of the tabernacles of the ungodly?
verses.29: Ask those that go by the way, and do not disown their tokens.
verses.30: For the wicked hastens to the day of destruction: they shall be led away for the day of his vengeance.
verses.31: Who will tell him his way to his face, whereas he has done it? who shall recompense him?
verses.32: And he has been led away to the tombs, and he has watched over the heaps.
verses.33: The stones of the valley have been sweet to him, and every man shall depart after him, and there are innumerable ones before him.
verses.34: How then do ye comfort me in vain? whereas I have no rest from your molestation.

verses.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
verses.2: Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise may be profitable unto himself?
verses.3: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or is it gain to him, that thou makest thy ways perfect?
verses.4: Will he reprove thee for fear of thee? will he enter with thee into judgment?
verses.5: Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?
verses.6: For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
verses.7: Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.
verses.8: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it.
verses.9: Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
verses.10: Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;
verses.11: Or darkness, that thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.
verses.12: Is not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!
verses.13: And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?
verses.14: Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.
verses.15: Hast thou marked the old way which wicked men have trodden?
verses.16: Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown with a flood:
verses.17: Which said unto God, Depart from us: and what can the Almighty do for them?
verses.18: Yet he filled their houses with good things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
verses.19: The righteous see it, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn.
verses.20: Whereas our substance is not cut down, but the remnant of them the fire consumeth.
verses.21: Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.
verses.22: Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.
verses.23: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles.
verses.24: Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.
verses.25: Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver.
verses.26: For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God.
verses.27: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows.
verses.28: Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways.
verses.29: When men are cast down, then thou shalt say, There is lifting up; and he shall save the humble person.
verses.30: He shall deliver the island of the innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands.

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἐλιφὰζ ὁ Θαιμανίτης, λέγει,
verses.2: Πότερον οὐχὶ ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν ὁ διδάσκων σύνεσιν καὶ ἐπιστήμην;
verses.3: Τί γὰρ μέλει τῷ Κυρίῳ, ἐὰν σὺ ἦσθα τοῖς ἔργοις ἄμεμπτος; ἢ ὠφέλεια, ὅτι ἀπλώσῃς τὴν ὁδόν σου;
verses.4: Ἢ λόγον σου ποιοῦμενος ἐλέγξεις, καὶ συνεισελεύσεταί σοι εἰς κρίσιν;
verses.5: Πότερον οὐχ ἡ κακία σου ἐστὶ πολλὴ, ἀναρίθμητοι δέ σου εἰσὶν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι;
verses.6: Ἠνεχύραζες δὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου διακενῆς, ἀμφίασιν δὲ γυμνῶν ἀφείλου.
verses.7: Οὐδὲ ὕδωρ διψῶντας ἐπότισας, ἀλλὰ πεινώντων ἐστέρησας ψωμόν·
verses.8: Ἐθαύμασας δέ τινων πρόσωπον, ᾤκισας δὲ τοὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
verses.9: Χήρας δὲ ἐξαπέστειλας κενὰς, ὀρφανοὺς δὲ ἐκάκωσας.
verses.10: Τοιγαροῦν ἐκύκλωσάν σε παγίδες, καὶ ἐσπούδασέ σε πόλεμος ἐξαίσιος.
verses.11: Τὸ φῶς σοι σκότος ἀπέβη, κοιμηθέντα δὲ ὕδωρ σε ἐκάλυψε.
verses.12: Μὴ οὐχὶ ὁ τὰ ὑψηλὰ ναίων ἐφορᾷ; τοὺς δὲ ὕβρει φερομένους ἐταπείνωσε;
verses.13: Καὶ εἶπας, τί ἔγνω ὁ ἰσχυρός; ἢ κατὰ τοῦ γνόφου κρίνει;
verses.14: Νεφέλη ἀποκρυφὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐχ ὁραθήσεται, καὶ γῦρον οὐρανοῦ διαπορεύεται.
verses.15: Μὴ τρίβον αἰώνιον φυλάξεις, ἣν ἐπάτησαν ἄνδρες δίκαιοι,
verses.16: οἳ συνελήφθησαν ἄωροι; ποταμὸς ἐπιῤῥέων οἱ θεμέλιοι αὐτῶν,

verses.1: Then Eliphaz the Thæmanite answered and said,
verses.2: Is it not the Lord that teaches understanding and knowledge?
verses.3: For what matters it to the Lord, if thou wert blameless in thy works? or is it profitable that thou shouldest perfect thy way?
verses.4: Wilt thou maintain and plead thine own cause? and will he enter into judgment with thee?
verses.5: Is not thy wickedness abundant, and thy sins innumerable?
verses.6: And thou hast taken security of thy brethren for nothing, and hast taken away the clothing of the naked.
verses.7: Neither hast thou given water to the thirsty to drink, but hast taken away the morsel of the hungry.
verses.8: And thou hast accepted the persons of some; and thou hast established those that were already settled on the earth.
verses.9: But thou hast sent widows away empty, and hast afflicted orphans.
verses.10: Therefore snares have compassed thee, and disastrous war has troubled thee.
verses.11: The light has proved darkness to thee, and water has covered thee on thy lying down.
verses.12: Does not he that dwells in the high places observe? and has he not brought down the proud?
verses.13: And thou hast said, What does the Mighty One know? does he judge in the dark?
verses.14: A cloud is his hiding-place, and he shall not be seen; and he passes through the circle of heaven.
verses.15: Wilt thou not mark the old way, which righteous men have trodden?
verses.16: who were seized before their time: their foundations are as an overflowing stream.
verses.17: Who say, What will the Lord do to us? or what will the Almighty bring upon us?
verses.18: Yet he filled their houses with good things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from him.
verses.19: The righteous have seen it, and laughed, and the blameless one has derided them.
verses.20: Verily their substance has been utterly destroyed, and the fire shall devour what is left of their property.
verses.21: Be firm, I pray thee, if thou canst endure; then thy fruit shall prosper.
verses.22: And receive a declaration from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.
verses.23: And if thou shalt turn and humble thyself before the Lord, thou hast thus removed unrighteousness far from thy habitation.
verses.24: Thou shalt lay up for thyself treasure in a heap on the rock; and Sophir shall be as the rock of the torrent.
verses.25: So the Almighty shall be thy helper from enemies, and he shall bring thee forth pure as silver that has been tried by fire.
verses.26: Then shalt thou have boldness before the Lord, looking up cheerfully to heaven.
verses.27: And he shall hear thee when thou prayest to him, and he shall grant thee power to pay thy vows.
verses.28: And he shall establish to thee again a habitation of righteousness and there shall be light upon thy paths.
verses.29: Because thou hast humbled thyself; and thou shalt say, Man has behaved proudly, but he shall save him that is of lowly eyes.
verses.30: He shall deliver the innocent, and do thou save thyself by thy pure hands.

verses.1: Then Job answered and said,
verses.2: Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.
verses.3: Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat!
verses.4: I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
verses.5: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.
verses.6: Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.
verses.7: There the righteous might dispute with him; so should I be delivered for ever from my judge.
verses.8: Behold, I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him:
verses.9: On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold him: he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see him:
verses.10: But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
verses.11: My foot hath held his steps, his way have I kept, and not declined.
verses.12: Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
verses.13: But he is in one mind, and who can turn him? and what his soul desireth, even that he doeth.
verses.14: For he performeth the thing that is appointed for me: and many such things are with him.
verses.15: Therefore am I troubled at his presence: when I consider, I am afraid of him.
verses.16: For God maketh my heart soft, and the Almighty troubleth me:
verses.17: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither hath he covered the darkness from my face.

verses.1: Then Job answered and said,

verses.15: Therefore am I troubled at him; and when I was reproved, I thought of him.
verses.15a: Therefore let me take good heed before him: I will consider, and be afraid of him.
verses.16: But the Lord has softened my heart, and the Almighty has troubled me.

verses.1: Why, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?
verses.2: Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed thereof.
verses.3: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
verses.4: They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together.
verses.5: Behold, as wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness yieldeth food for them and for their children.
verses.6: They reap every one his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.
verses.7: They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that they have no covering in the cold.
verses.8: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.
verses.9: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.
verses.10: They cause him to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf from the hungry;
verses.11: Which make oil within their walls, and tread their winepresses, and suffer thirst.
verses.12: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly to them.
verses.13: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof.
verses.14: The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.
verses.15: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.
verses.16: In the dark they dig through houses, which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.
verses.17: For the morning is to them even as the shadow of death: if one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.
verses.18: He is swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.
verses.19: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned.
verses.20: The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree.
verses.21: He evil entreateth the barren that beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.
verses.22: He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no man is sure of life.
verses.23: Though it be given him to be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes are upon their ways.
verses.24: They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.
verses.25: And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?

verses.1: But why have the seasons been hidden from the Lord,
verses.2: while the ungodly have passed over the bound, carrying off the flock with the shepherd?
verses.3: They have led away the ass of the fatherless, and taken the widow's ox for a pledge.
verses.4: They have turned aside the weak from the right way: and the meek of the earth have hidden themselves together.
verses.5: And they have departed like asses in the field, having gone forth on my account according to their own order: his bread is sweet to his little ones.
verses.6: They have reaped a field that was not their own before the time: the poor have laboured in the vineyards of the ungodly without pay and without food.
verses.7: They have caused many naked to sleep without clothes, and they have taken away the covering of their body.
verses.8: They are wet with the drops of the mountains: they have embraced the rock, because they had no shelter.
verses.9: They have snatched the fatherless from the breast, and have afflicted the outcast.
verses.10: And they have wrongfully caused others to sleep without clothing, and taken away the morsel of the hungry.
verses.11: They have unrighteously laid wait in narrow places, and have not known the righteous way.
verses.12: Who have cast forth the poor from the city and their own houses, and the soul of the children has groaned aloud.
verses.13: Why then has he not visited these? forasmuch as they were upon the earth, and took no notice, and they knew not the way of righteousness, neither have they walked in their appointed paths?

verses.16: In darkness he digs through houses: by day they conceal themselves securely: they know not the light.
verses.17: For the morning is to them all as the shadow of death, for each will be conscious of the terror of the shadow of death.
verses.18: He is swift on the face of the water: let his portion be cursed on the earth; and let their plants be laid bare.
verses.19: Let them be withered upon the earth; for they have plundered the sheaves of the fatherless.
verses.20: Then is his sin brought to remembrance, and he vanishes like a vapour of dew: but let what he has done be recompensed to him, and let every unrighteous one be crushed like rotten wood.

verses.22: And in wrath he has overthrown the helpless: therefore when he has arisen, a man will not feel secure of his own life.
verses.23: When he has fallen sick, let him not hope to recover: but let him perish by disease.
verses.24: For his exaltation has hurt many; but he has withered as mallows in the heat, or as an ear of corn falling off of itself from the stalk.
verses.25: But if not, who is he that says I speak falsely, and will make my words of no account?

verses.7: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.
verses.8: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?
verses.9: Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?
verses.10: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God?
verses.11: I will teach you by the hand of God: that which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.
verses.12: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; why then are ye thus altogether vain?
verses.13: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, which they shall receive of the Almighty.
verses.14: If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.
verses.15: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.
verses.16: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay;
verses.17: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.
verses.18: He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth that the keeper maketh.
verses.19: The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he is not.
verses.20: Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.
verses.21: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place.
verses.22: For God shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.
verses.23: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

verses.1: Ἔτι δὲ προσθεὶς Ἰὼβ εἶπεν τῷ προοιμίῳ,
verses.2: Ζῇ ὁ Θεὸς, ὃς οὕτω με κέκρικε, καὶ ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὁ πικράνας μου τὴν ψυχὴν,
verses.3: εἰ μὴν ἔτι τῆς πνοῆς μου ἐνούσης, πνεῦμα δὲ θεῖον τὸ περιόν μοι ἐν ῥινὶ,
verses.4: μὴ λαλήσειν τὰ χείλη μου ὄνομα, οὐδὲ ἡ ψυχή μου μελετήσει ἄδικα.
verses.5: Μή μοι εἴη δικαίους ὑμᾶς ἀποφῆναι ἕως ἂν ἀποθάνω, οὐ γὰρ ἀπαλλάξω μου τὴν ἀκακίαν μου.
verses.6: Δικαιοσύνῃ δὲ προσέχων οὐ μὴν προῶμαι, οὐ γὰρ σύνοιδα ἐμαυτῷ ἄτοπα πράξας.
verses.7: Οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ εἴησαν οἱ ἐχθροί μου ὥσπερ ἡ καταστροφὴ τῶν ἀσεβῶν, καὶ οἱ ἐπʼ ἐμὲ ἐπανιστάμενοι, ὥσπερ ἡ ἀπώλεια τῶν παρανόμων.
verses.8: Καὶ τίς γάρ ἐστιν ἐλπὶς ἀσεβεῖ, ὅτι ἐπέχει; πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ κύριον ἄρα σωθήσεται;
verses.9: Ἢ τὴν δέησιν αὐτοῦ εἰσακούσεται ὁ Θεός; ἢ ἐπελθούσης αὐτῷ ἀνάγκης
verses.10: μὴ ἔχει τινὰ παῤῥησίαν ἔναντι αὐτοῦ; ἢ ὡς ἐπικαλεσαμένου αὐτοῦ εἰσακούσεται αὐτοῦ;
verses.11: Ἀλλὰ δὴ ἀναγγελῶ ὑμῖν τί ἐστιν ἐν χειρὶ Κυρίου, ἅ ἐστι παρὰ παντοκράτορι, οὐ ψεύσομαι.
verses.12: Ἰδοὺ πάντες οἴδατε, ὅτι κενὰ κενοῖς ἐπιβάλλετε.
verses.13: Αὕτη ἡ μερὶς ἀνθρώπου ἀσεβοῦς παρὰ Κυρίου, κτῆμα δὲ δυναστῶν ἐλεύσεται παρὰ παντοκράτορος ἐπʼ αὐτούς.
verses.14: Ἐὰν δἐ πολλοὶ γένωνται οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτῶν, εἰς σφαγὴν ἔσονται· ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἀνδρωθῶσι, προσαιτήσουσιν.
verses.15: Οἱ δὲ περιόντες αὐτοῦ ἐν θανάτῳ τελευτήσουσι, χήρας δὲ αὐτῶν οὐδεὶς ἐλεήσει.
verses.16: Ἐὰν συναγάγῃ ὥσπερ γῆν ἀργύριον, ἶσα δὲ πηλῷ ἑτοιμάσῃ χρυσίον,
verses.17: ταῦτα πάντα δίκαιοι περιποιήσονται, τὰ δὲ χρήματα αὐτοῦ ἀληθινοὶ καθέξουσιν.
verses.18: Ἀπέβη δὲ ὁ οἶκος αὐτοῦ ὥσπερ σῆτες, καὶ ὥσπερ ἀράχνη.
verses.19: Πλούσιος κοιμηθήσεται καὶ οὐ προσθήσει, ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ διήνοιξε καὶ οὐκ ἔστι.
verses.20: Συνήντησαν αὐτῷ ὥσπερ ὕδωρ αἱ ὀδύναι, νυκτὶ δὲ ὑφείλατο αὐτὸν γνόφος.
verses.21: Ἀναλήψεται δὲ αὐτὸν καύσων καὶ ἀπελεύσεται, καὶ λικμήσει αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτοῦ.
verses.22: Καὶ ἐπιῤῥίψει ἐπʼ αὐτὸν καὶ οὐ φείσεται, ἐκ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ φυγῇ φεύξεται.
verses.23: Κροτήσει ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς χεῖρας αὐτῶν, καὶ συριεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτοῦ.

verses.1: And Job further continued and said in his parable,
verses.2: As God lives, who has thus judged me; and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul;
verses.3: verily, while my breath is yet in me, and the breath of God which remains to me is in my nostrils,
verses.4: my lips shall not speak evil words, neither shall my soul meditate unrighteous thoughts.
verses.5: Far be it from me that I should justify you till I die; for I will not let go my innocence,
verses.6: but keeping fast to my righteousness I will by no means let it go: for I am not conscious to myself of having done any thing amiss.
verses.7: Nay rather, but let mine enemies be as the overthrow of the ungodly, and they that rise up against me, as the destruction of transgressors.
verses.8: For what is the hope of the ungodly, that he holds to it? will he indeed trust in the Lord and be saved?
verses.9: Will God hear his prayer? or, when distress has come upon him,
verses.10: has he any confidence before him? or will God hear him as he calls upon him?
verses.11: Yet now I will tell you what is in the hand of the Lord: I will not lie concerning the things which are with the Almighty.
verses.12: Behold, ye all know that ye are adding vanity to vanity.
verses.13: This is the portion of an ungodly man from the Lord, and the possession of oppressors shall come upon them from the Almighty.
verses.14: And if their children be many, they shall be for slaughter: and if they grow up, they shall beg.
verses.15: And they that survive of him shall utterly perish, and no one shall pity their widows.
verses.16: Even if he should gather silver as earth, and prepare gold as clay;
verses.17: all these things shall the righteous gain, and the truehearted shall possess his wealth.
verses.18: And his house is gone like moths, and like a spider's web.
verses.19: The rich man shall lie down, and shall not continue: he has opened his eyes, and he is not.
verses.20: Pains have come upon him as water, and darkness has carried him away by night.
verses.21: And a burning wind shall catch him, and he shall depart, and it shall utterly drive him out of his place.
verses.22: And God shall cast trouble upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.
verses.23: He shall cause men to clap their hands against them, and shall hiss him out of his place.

verses.1: Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it.
verses.2: Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone.
verses.3: He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death.
verses.4: The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; even the waters forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men.
verses.5: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.
verses.6: The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.
verses.7: There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture’s eye hath not seen:
verses.8: The lion’s whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.
verses.9: He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.
verses.10: He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.
verses.11: He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.
verses.12: But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?
verses.13: Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.
verses.14: The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me.
verses.15: It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.
verses.16: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
verses.17: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold.
verses.18: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies.
verses.19: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
verses.20: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?
verses.21: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.
verses.22: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.
verses.23: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.
verses.24: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven;
verses.25: To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.
verses.26: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:
verses.27: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.
verses.28: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.

verses.1: Ἐστι γὰρ ἀργυρίῳ τόπος ὅθεν γίνεται, τόπος δὲ χρυσίου ὅθεν διηθεῖται.
verses.2: Σίδηρος μὲν γὰρ ἐκ γῆς γίνεται, χαλκὸς δὲ ἶσα λίθῳ λατομεῖται.
verses.3: Τάξιν ἔθετο σκότει, καὶ πᾶν πέρας αὐτὸς ἐξακριβάζεται, λίθος σκοτία, καὶ σκιὰ θανάτου.
verses.4: Διακοπὴ χειμάῤῥου ἀπὸ κονίας, οἱ δὲ ἐπιλανθανόμενοι ὁδὸν δικαίαν ἠσθένησαν, ἐκ βροτῶν ἐσαλεύθησαν.
verses.5: Γῆ, ἐξ αὐτῆς ἐξελεύσεται ἄρτος, ὑποκάτω αὐτῆς ἐστράφη ὡσεὶ πῦρ.
verses.6: Τόπος σαπφείρου οἱ λίθοι αὐτῆς, καὶ χῶμα χρυσίον αὐτῷ.
verses.7: Τρίβος, οὐκ ἔγνω αὐτὴν πετεινὸν, καὶ οὐ παρέβλεψεν αὐτὴν ὀφθαλμὸς γυπός·
verses.8: Καὶ οὐκ ἐπάτησαν αὐτὸν υἱοὶ ἀλαζόνων, οὐ παρῆλθεν ἐπʼ αὐτῆς λέων.
verses.9: Ἐν ἀκροτόμῳ ἐξέτεινε χεῖρα αὐτοῦ, κατέστρεψε δὲ ἐκ ῥιζῶν ὄρη.
verses.10: Δίνας δὲ ποταμῶν διέῤῥηξε, πᾶν δὲ ἔντιμον εἴδέ μου ὁ ὀφθαλμός.
verses.11: Βάθη δὲ ποταμῶν ἀνεκάλυψεν, ἔδειξε δὲ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν εἰς φῶς.
verses.12: Ἡ δὲ σοφία πόθεν εὑρέθη; ποῖος δὲ τόπος ἐστὶ τῆς ἐπιστήμης;
verses.13: Οὐκ οἶδε βροτὸς ὁδὸν αὐτῆς, οὐδὲ μὴν εὑρέθη ἐν ἀνθρώποις.
verses.14: Ἄβυσσος εἶπεν, οὐκ ἔνεστιν ἐν ἐμοί· καὶ ἡ θάλασσα εἶπεν, οὐκ ἔνεστι μετʼ ἐμοῦ.
verses.15: Οὐ δώσει συνκλεισμὸν ἀντʼ αὐτῆς, καὶ οὐ σταθήσεται ἀργύριον ἀντάλλαγμα αὐτῆς.
verses.16: Καὶ οὐ συνβασταχθήσεται χρυσίῳ Σωφεὶρ, ἐν ὄνυχι τιμίῳ καὶ σαπφείρῳ.
verses.17: Οὐκ ἰσωθήσεται αὐτῇ χρυσίον καὶ ὕαλος, καὶ τὸ ἄλλαγμα αὐτῆς σκεύη χρυσᾶ.
verses.18: Μετέωρα καὶ γαβὶς οὐ μνησθήσεται, καὶ ἕλκυσον σοφίαν ὑπὲρ τὰ ἐσώτατα.
verses.19: Οὐκ ἰσωθήσεται αὐτῇ τοπάζιον Αἰθιοπίας, χρυσίῳ καθαρῷ οὐ συμβασταχθήσεται.
verses.20: Ἡ δὲ σοφία πόθεν εὑρέθη; ποῖος δὲ τόπος ἐστὶ τῆς συνέσεως;
verses.21: Λέληθε πάντα ἄνθρωπον, καὶ ἀπὸ πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐκρύβη.
verses.22: Ἡ ἀπώλεια καὶ ὁ θάνατος εἶπαν, ἀκηκόαμεν δὲ αὐτῆς τὸ κλέος.
verses.23: Ὁ Θεὸς εὖ συνέστησεν αὐτῆς τὴν ὁδὸν, αὐτὸς δὲ οἶδε τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς.
verses.24: Αὐτὸς γὰρ τὴν ὑπʼ οὐρανὸν πᾶσαν ἐφορᾷ· εἰδὼς τὰ ἐν τῇ γῇ, πάντα
verses.25: ἃ ἐποίησεν, ἀνέμων σταθμὸν, ὕδατος μέτρα ὅτε ἐποίησεν·
verses.26: οὕτως ἰδὼν ἠρίθμησε, καὶ ὁδὸν ἐν τινάγματι φωνάς.
verses.27: Τότε εἶδεν αὐτὴν, καὶ ἐξηγήσατο αὐτὴν, ἑτοιμάσας ἐξιχνίασεν.
verses.28: Εἶπε δὲ ἀνθρώπῳ, Ἰδοὺ ἡ θεοσέβειά ἐστι σοφία, τὸ δὲ ἀπέχεσθαι ἀπὸ κακῶν ἐστὶν ἐπιστήμη.

verses.1: For there is a place for the silver, whence it comes, and a place for the gold, whence it is refined.
verses.2: For iron comes out of the earth, and brass is hewn out like stone.
verses.3: He has set a bound to darkness, and he searches out every limit: a stone is darkness, and the shadow of death.
verses.4: There is a cutting off of the torrent by reason of dust: so they that forget the right way are weakened; they are removed from among men.
verses.5: As for the earth, out of it shall come bread: under it has been turned up as it were fire.
verses.6: Her stones are the place of the sapphire: and her dust supplies man with gold.
verses.7: There is a path, the fowl has not known it, neither has the eye of the vulture seen it:
verses.8: neither have the sons of the proud trodden it, a lion has not passed upon it.
verses.9: He has stretched forth his hand on the sharp rock, and turned up mountains by the roots:
verses.10: and he has interrupted the whirlpools of rivers, and mine eye has seen every precious thing.
verses.11: And he has laid bare the depths of rivers, and has brought his power to light.
verses.12: But whence has wisdom been discovered? and what is the place of knowledge?
verses.13: A mortal has not known its way, neither indeed has it been discovered among men.
verses.14: The depth said, It is not in me: and the sea said, It is not with me.
verses.15: One shall not give fine gold instead of it, neither shall silver be weighed in exchange for it.
verses.16: Neither shall it be compared with gold of Sophir, with the precious onyx and sapphire.
verses.17: Gold and crystal shall not be equalled to it, neither shall vessels of gold be its exchange.
verses.18: Coral and fine pearl shall not be mentioned: but do thou esteem wisdom above the most precious things.
verses.19: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not be equalled to it; it shall not be compared with pure gold.
verses.20: Whence then is wisdom found? and of what kind is the place of understanding?
verses.21: It has escaped the notice of every man, and has been hidden from the birds of the sky.
verses.22: Destruction and Death said, We have heard the report of it.
verses.23: God has well ordered the way of it, and he knows the place of it.
verses.24: For he surveys the whole earth under heaven, knowing the things in the earth:
verses.25: all that he has made; the weight of the winds, the measures of the water.
verses.26: When he made them, thus he saw and numbered them, and made a way for the pealing of the thunder.
verses.27: Then he saw it, and declared it: he prepared it and traced it out.
verses.28: And he said to man, Behold, godliness is wisdom; and to abstain from evil is understanding.

verses.1: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.
verses.2: Yea, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?
verses.3: For want and famine they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.
verses.4: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat.
verses.5: They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)
verses.6: To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.
verses.7: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.
verses.8: They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.
verses.9: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.
verses.10: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.
verses.11: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.
verses.12: Upon my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.
verses.13: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.
verses.14: They came upon me as a wide breaking in of waters: in the desolation they rolled themselves upon me.
verses.15: Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud.
verses.16: And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.
verses.17: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.
verses.18: By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.
verses.19: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.
verses.20: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not.
verses.21: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.
verses.22: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride upon it, and dissolvest my substance.
verses.23: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living.
verses.24: Howbeit he will not stretch out his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.
verses.25: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?
verses.26: When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
verses.27: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.
verses.28: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation.
verses.29: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.
verses.30: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.
verses.31: My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

verses.1: Νυνὶ δὲ κατεγέλασάν μου ἐλάχιστοι, νῦν νουθετοῦσί με ἐν μέρει, ὧν ἐξουδένουν τοὺς πατέρας αὐτῶν, οὓς οὐχ ἡγησάμην ἀξίους κυνῶν τῶν ἐμῶν νομάδων.
verses.2: Καί γε ἰσχὺς χειρῶν αὐτῶν ἱνατί μοι; ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ἀπώλετο συντέλεια.
verses.3: Ἐν ἐνδείᾳ καὶ λιμῷ ἄγονος, οἱ φεύγοντες ἄνυδρον ἐχθὲς συνοχὴν καὶ ταλαιπωρίαν.
verses.4: Οἱ περικυκλοῦντες ἄλιμα ἐπὶ ἠχοῦντι, οἵτινες ἄλιμα ἦν αὐτῶν τὰ σῖτα, ἄτιμοι δὲ καὶ πεφαυλισμένοι, ἐνδεεῖς παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ, οἳ καὶ ῥὶζας ξύλων ἐμασσῶντο ὑπὸ λιμοῦ μεγάλου.
verses.5: Ἐπανέστησάν μοι κλέπται,
verses.6: ὧν οἱ οἶκοι αὐτῶν ἦσαν τρῶγλαι πετρῶν·
verses.7: Ἀναμέσον εὐήχων βοήσονται οἳ ὑπὸ φρύγανα ἄγρια διῃτῶντο.
verses.8: Ἀφρόνων υἱοὶ καὶ ἀτίμων, ὄνομα καὶ κλέος ἐσβεσμένον ἀπὸ γῆς.
verses.9: Νυνὶ δὲ κιθάρα ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐμὲ θρύλλημα ἔχουσιν.
verses.10: Ἐβδελύξαντο δέ με ἀποστάντες μακρὰν, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ προσώπου μου οὐκ ἐφείσαντο πτύελον.
verses.11: Ἀνοίξας γὰρ φαρέτραν αὐτοῦ ἐκάκωσέ με, καὶ χαλινὸν τοῦ προσώπου μου ἐξαπέστειλεν.
verses.12: Ἐπὶ δεξιῶν βλαστοῦ ἐπανέστησαν, πόδα αὐτῶν ἐξέτειναν, καὶ ὡδοποίησαν ἐπʼ ἐμὲ· τρίβους ἀπωλείας αὐτῶν.
verses.13: Ἐξετρίβησαν τρίβοι μου, ἐξέδυσαν γάρ μου τὴν στολήν·
verses.14: βέλεσιν αὐτοῦ κατηκόντισέ με. Κέκριται δέ μοι ὡς βούλεται, ἐν ὀδύναις πέφυρμαι.
verses.15: Ἐπιστρέφονταί μου αἱ ὀδύναι, ᾤχετό μου ἡ ἐλπὶς ὥσπερ πνεῦμα, καὶ ὥσπερ νέφος ἡ σωτηρία μου.
verses.16: Καὶ νῦν ἐπʼ ἐμὲ ἐκχυθήσεται ἡ ψυχή μου, ἔχουσιν δέ με ἡμέραι ὀδυνῶν.
verses.17: Νυκτὶ δέ μου τὰ ὀστᾶ συγκέχυται, τὰ δὲ νεῦρά μου διαλέλυται.
verses.18: Ἐν πολλῇ ἰσχύϊ ἐπελάβετό μου τῆς στολῆς, ὥσπερ τὸ περιστόμιον τοῦ χιτῶνός μου περιέσχε με.
verses.19: Ἥγησαι δέ με ἴσα πηλῷ, ἐν γῇ καὶ σποδῷ μου ἡ μερίς.
verses.20: Κέκραγα δὲ πρὸς σὲ καὶ οὐκ ἀκούεις μου, ἔστησαν δὲ καὶ κατενόησάν με.
verses.21: Ἐπέβησαν δέ μοι ἀνελεημόνως, χειρὶ κραταιᾷ με ἐμαστίγωσας.
verses.22: Ἔταξας δέ με ἐν ὀδύναις, καὶ ἀπέῤῥιψάς με ἀπὸ σωτηρίας.
verses.23: Οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι θάνατός με ἐκτρίψει, οἰκία γὰρ παντὶ θνητῷ γῆ.
verses.24: Εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον δυναίμην ἐμαυτὸν χειρώσασθαι, ἢ δεηθείς γε ἑτέρου, καὶ ποιήσει μοι τοῦτο.
verses.25: Ἐγὼ δὲ ἐπὶ παντὶ ἀδυνάτῳ ἔκλαυσα, ἐστέναξα ἰδὼν ἄνδρα ἐν ἀνάγκαις·
verses.26: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐπέχων ἀγαθοῖς, ἰδοὺ συνήντησάν μοι μᾶλλον ἡμέραι κακῶν.
verses.27: Ἡ κοιλία μου ἐξέζεσε καὶ οὐ σιωπήσεται, προέφθασάν με ἡμέραι πτωχείας.
verses.28: Στένων πεπόρευμαι ἄνευ φιμοῦ, ἕστηκα δὲ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ κεκραγώς.
verses.29: Ἀδελφὸς γέγονα σειρήνων, ἑταῖρος δὲ στρουθῶν.
verses.30: Τὸ δὲ δέρμα μου ἐσκότωται μεγάλως, τὰ δὲ ὀστᾶ μου ἀπὸ καύματος.
verses.31: Ἀπέβη δὲ εἰς πένθος μου ἡ κιθάρα, ὁ δὲ ψαλμός μου εἰς κλαυθμὸν ἐμοί.

verses.1: But now the youngest have laughed me to scorn, now they reprove me in their turn, whose fathers I set at nought; whom I did not deem worthy to be with my shepherd dogs.
verses.2: Yea, why had I the strength of their hands? for them the full term of life was lost.
verses.3: One is childless in want and famine, such as they that fled but lately the distress and misery of drought.
verses.4: Who compass the salt places on the sounding shore, who had salt herbs for their food, and were dishonourable and of no repute, in want of every good thing; who also ate roots of trees by reason of great hunger.
verses.5: Thieves have risen up against me,
verses.6: whose houses were the caves of the rocks, who lived under the wild shrubs.
verses.7: They will cry out among the rustling bushes.
verses.8: They are sons of fools and vile men, whose name and glory are quenched from off the earth.
verses.9: But now I am their music, and they have me for a by-word.
verses.10: And they stood aloof and abhorred me, and spared not to spit in my face.
verses.11: For he has opened his quiver and afflicted me: they also have cast off the restraint of my presence.
verses.12: They have risen up against me on the right hand of their offspring; they have stretched out their foot, and directed against me the ways of their destruction.
verses.13: My paths are ruined; for they have stripped off my raiment: he has shot at me with his weapons.
verses.14: And he has pleaded against me as he will: I am overwhelmed with pains.
verses.15: My pains return upon me; my hope is gone like the wind, and my safety as a cloud.
verses.16: Even now my life shall be poured forth upon me; and days of anguish seize me.
verses.17: And by night my bones are confounded; and my sinews are relaxed.
verses.18: With great force my disease has taken hold of my garment: it has compassed me as the collar of my coat.
verses.19: And thou hast counted me as clay; my portion is in dust and ashes.
verses.20: And I have cried to thee, but thou hearest me not: but they stood still, and observed me.
verses.21: They attacked me also without mercy: thou hast scourged me with a strong hand.
verses.22: And thou hast put me to grief, and hast cast me away from safety.
verses.23: For I know that death will destroy me: for the earth is the house appointed for every mortal.
verses.24: Oh then that I might lay hands upon myself, or at least ask another, and he should do this for me.
verses.25: Yet I wept over every helpless man; I groaned when I saw a man in distress.
verses.26: But I, when I waited for good things, behold, days of evils came the more upon me.
verses.27: My belly boiled, and would not cease: the days of poverty prevented me.
verses.28: I went mourning without restraint: and I have stood and cried out in the assembly.
verses.29: I am become a brother of monsters, and a companion of ostriches.
verses.30: And my skin has been greatly blackened, and my bones are burned with heat.
verses.31: My harp also has been turned into mourning, and my song into my weeping.

verses.1: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
verses.2: For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
verses.3: Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?
verses.4: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?
verses.5: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;
verses.6: Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity.
verses.7: If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;
verses.8: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.
verses.9: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door;
verses.10: Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.
verses.11: For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.
verses.12: For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.
verses.13: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;
verses.14: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?
verses.15: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?
verses.16: If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;
verses.17: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;
verses.18: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother’s womb;)
verses.19: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;
verses.20: If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
verses.21: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:
verses.22: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.
verses.23: For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.
verses.24: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;
verses.25: If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;
verses.26: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;
verses.27: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:
verses.28: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above.
verses.29: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:
verses.30: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.
verses.31: If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.
verses.32: The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller.
verses.33: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:
verses.34: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door?
verses.35: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that mine adversary had written a book.
verses.36: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me.
verses.37: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.
verses.38: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;
verses.39: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:
verses.40: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

verses.1: Διαθήκην ἐθέμην τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς μου, καὶ οὐ συνήσω ἐπὶ παρθένον.
verses.2: Καὶ τί ἐμέρισεν ὁ Θεὸς ἄνωθεν, καὶ κληρονομία ἱκανοῦ ἐξ ὑψίστων;
verses.3: Οὐαί, ἀπώλεια τῷ ἀδίκῳ, καὶ ἀπαλλοτρίωσις τοῖς ποιοῦσιν ἀνομίαν.
verses.4: Οὐχὶ αὐτὸς ὄψεται ὁδόν μου, καὶ πάντα τὰ διαβήματά μου ἐξαριθμήσεται;
verses.5: Εἰ δὲ ἤμην πεπορευμένος μετὰ γελοιαστῶν, εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐσπούδασεν ὁ πούς μου εἰς δόλον·
verses.6: Ἕσταμαι γὰρ ἐν ζυγῷ δικαίῳ, οἶδε δὲ ὁ Κύριος τὴν ἀκακίαν μου·
verses.7: Εἰ ἐξέκλινεν ὁ πούς μου ἐκ τῆς ὁδοῦ, εἰ δὲ καὶ τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ ἐπηκολούθησεν ἡ καρδία μου, εἰ δὲ καὶ ταῖς χερσί μου ἡψάμην δώρων,
verses.8: σπείραιμι ἄρα καὶ ἄλλοι φάγοισαν, ἄῤῥιζος δὲ γενοίμην ἐπὶ γῆς.
verses.9: Εἰ ἐξηκολούθησεν ἡ καρδία μου γυναικὶ ἀνδρὸς ἑτέρου, εἰ καὶ ἐγκάθετος ἐγενόμην ἐπὶ θύραις αὐτῆς,
verses.10: ἀρέσαι ἄρα καὶ ἡ γυνή μου ἑτέρῳ, τὰ δὲ νήπιά μου ταπεινωθείη.
verses.11: Θυμὸς γὰρ ὀργῆς ἀκατάσχετος, τὸ μιᾶναι ἀνδρὸς γυναῖκα.
verses.12: Πῦρ γάρ ἐστι καιόμενον ἐπὶ πάντων τῶν μερῶν, οὗδʼ ἂν ἐπέλθῃ ἐκ ῥιζῶν ἀπώλεσεν.
verses.13: Εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐφαύλισα κρίμα θεράποντός μου ἢ θεραπαίνης, κρινομένων αὐτῶν πρὸς μὲ,
verses.14: τί γὰρ ποιήσω ἐὰν ἔτασίν μου ποιῆται ὁ Κύριος; ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἐπισκοπήν τινα, ἀπόκρισιν ποιήσομαι;
verses.15: Πότερον οὐχ ὡς καὶ ἐγὼ ἐγενόμην ἐν γαστρὶ, καὶ ἐκεῖνοι γεγόνασι; γεγόναμεν δὲ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ κοιλίᾳ.
verses.16: Ἀδύνατοι δὲ χρείαν ἥν ποτε εἶχον οὐκ ἀπέτυχον, χήρας δὲ τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν οὐκ ἐξέτηξα·
verses.17: Εἰ δὲ καὶ τὸν ψωμόν μου ἔφαγον μόνος, καὶ οὐχὶ ὀρφανῷ μετέδωκα·
verses.18: Ὅτι ἐκ νεότητός μου ἐξέτρεφον ὡς πατὴρ, καὶ ἐκ γαστρὸς μητρός μου ὡδήγησα·
verses.19: Εἰ δὲ καὶ ὑπερεῖδον γυμνὸν ἀπολλύμενον, καὶ οὐκ ἠμφίασα αὐτόν·
verses.20: Ἀδύνατοι δὲ εἰ μὴ εὐλόγησάν με, ἀπὸ δὲ κουρᾶς ἀμνῶν μοῦ ἐθερμάνθησαν οἱ ὦμοι αὐτῶν·
verses.21: Εἰ ἐπῆρα ὀρφανῷ χεῖρα, πεποιθὼς ὅτι πολλή μοι βοήθεια περίεστιν·
verses.22: Ἀποσταίη ἄρα ὁ ὦμός μου ἀπὸ τῆς κλειδός, ὁ δὲ βραχίων μου ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀγκῶνος συντριβείη.
verses.23: Φόβος γὰρ Κυρίου συνέσχε με, ἀπὸ τοῦ λήμματος αὐτοῦ οὐχ ὑποίσω.
verses.24: Εἰ ἔταξα χρυσίον εἰς χοῦν μου, εἰ δὲ καὶ λίθῳ πολυτελεῖ ἐπεποίθησα,
verses.25: εἰ δὲ καὶ εὐφράνθην πολλοῦ πλούτου μου γενομένου, εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐπʼ ἀναριθμήτοις ἐθέμην χεῖρά μου·
verses.26: Ἢ οὐχ ὁρῶμεν ἥλιον τὸν ἐπιθαύσκοντα ἐκλείποντα, σελήνην δὲ φθίνουσαν; οὐ γὰρ ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς ἐστί·
verses.27: Καὶ εἰ ἠπατήθη λάθρα ἡ καρδία μου, εἰ δὲ χεῖρά μου ἐπιθεὶς ἐπὶ στόματί μου ἐφίλησα.
verses.28: Καὶ τοῦτό μοι ἄρα ἀνομία ἡ μεγίστη λογισθείη, ὅτι ἐψευσάμην ἐναντίον Κυρίου τοῦ ὑψίστου.
verses.29: Εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐπιχαρὴς ἐγενόμην πτώματι ἐχθρῶν μου, καὶ εἶπεν ἡ καρδία μου, εὖγε.
verses.30: Ἀκούσαι ἄρα τὸ οὖς μου τὴν κατάραν μου, θρυληθείην δὲ ἄρα ὑπὸ λαοῦ μου κακούμενος.
verses.31: Εἰ δὲ καὶ πολλάκις εἶπον αἱ θεράπαιναί μου, τίς ἄν δῴη ἡμῖν τῶν σαρκῶν αὐτοῦ πλησθῆναι; λίαν μου χρηστοῦ ὄντος·
verses.32: Ἔξω δὲ οὐκ ηὐλίζετο ξένος, ἡ δὲ θύρα μου παντὶ ἐλθόντι ἀνέῳκτο·
verses.33: Εἰ δὲ καὶ ἁμαρτὼν ἀκουσίως ἔκρυψα τὴν ἁμαρτίαν μου·
verses.34: Οὐ γὰρ διετράπην πολυοχλίαν πλήθους, τοῦ μὴ ἐξαγορεῦσαι ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν· εἰ δὲ καὶ εἴασα ἀδύνατον ἐξελθεῖν θύραν μου κόλπῳ κενῷ·
verses.35: Τίς δῴη ἀκούοντά μου; χεῖρα δὲ Κυρίου εἰ μὴ ἐδεδοίκειν· συγγραφὴν δὲ ἣν εἶχον κατά τινος,
verses.36: ἐπʼ ὤμοις ἂν περιθέμενος στέφανον ἀνεγίνωσκον,
verses.37: καὶ εἰ μὴ ῥῆξας αὐτὴν ἀπέδωκα, οὐθὲν λαβὼν παρὰ χρεωφειλέτου·
verses.38: Εἰ ἐπʼ ἐμοί ποτε ἡ γῆ ἐστέναξεν, εἰ δὲ καὶ οἱ αὔλακες αὐτῆς ἔκλαυσαν ὁμοθυμαδόν·
verses.39: Εἰ δὲ καὶ τὴν ἰσχὺν αὐτῆς ἔφαγον μόνος ἄνευ τιμῆς, εἰ δὲ καὶ ψυχὴν κυρίου τῆς γῆς ἐκλαβὼν ἐλύπησα·
verses.40: Ἀντὶ πυροῦ ἄρα ἐξέλθοι μοι κνίδη, ἀντὶ δὲ κριθῆς βάτος. Καὶ ἐπαύσατο Ἰὼβ ῥήμασιν.

verses.1: I made a covenant with mine eyes, and I will not think upon a virgin.
verses.2: Now what portion has God given from above? and is there an inheritance given of the Mighty One from the highest?
verses.3: Alas! destruction to the unrighteous, and rejection to them that do iniquity.
verses.4: Will he not see my way, and number all my steps?
verses.5: But if I had gone with scorners, and if too my foot has hasted to deceit:
verses.6: (for I am weighed in a just balance, and the Lord knows my innocence:)
verses.7: if my foot has turned aside out of the way, or if mine heart has followed mine eye, and if too I have touched gifts with my hands;
verses.8: then let me sow, and let others eat; and let me be uprooted on the earth.
verses.9: If my heart has gone forth after another man's wife, and if I laid wait at her doors;
verses.10: then let my wife also please another, and let my children be brought low.
verses.11: For the rage of anger is not to be controlled, in the case of defiling another man's wife.
verses.12: For it is a fire burning on every side, and whomsoever it attacks, it utterly destroys.
verses.13: And if too I despised the judgment of my servant or my handmaid, when they pleaded with me;
verses.14: what then shall I do if the Lord should try me? and if also he should at all visit me, can I make an answer?
verses.15: Were not they too formed as I also was formed in the womb? yea, we were formed in the same womb.
verses.16: But the helpless missed not whatever need they had, and I did not cause the eye of the widow to fail.
verses.17: And if too I ate my morsel alone, and did not impart of it to the orphan;
verses.18: (for I nourished them as a father from my youth, and guided them from my mother's womb.)
verses.19: And if too I overlooked the naked as he was perishing, and did not clothe him;
verses.20: and if the poor did not bless me, and their shoulders were not warmed with the fleece of my lambs;
verses.21: if I lifted my hand against an orphan, trusting that my strength was far superior to his:
verses.22: let then my shoulder start from the blade-bone, and my arm be crushed off from the elbow.
verses.23: For the fear of the Lord constrained me, and I cannot bear up by reason of his burden.
verses.24: If I made gold my treasure, and if too I trusted the precious stone;
verses.25: and if too I rejoiced when my wealth was abundant, and if too I laid my hand on innumerable treasures:
verses.26: (do we not see the shining sun eclipsed, and the moon waning? for they have not power to continue:)
verses.27: and if my heart was secretly deceived, and if I have laid my hand upon my mouth and kissed it:
verses.28: let this also then be reckoned to me as the greatest iniquity: for I should have lied against the Lord Most High.
verses.29: And if too I was glad at the fall of mine enemies, and mine heart said, Aha!
verses.30: let then mine ear hear my curse, and let me be a by-word among my people in my affliction.
verses.31: And if too my handmaids have often said, Oh that we might be satisfied with his flesh; (whereas I was very kind:
verses.32: for the stranger did not lodge without, and my door was opened to every one that came:)
verses.33: or if too having sinned unintentionally, I hid my sin;
verses.34: (for I did not stand in awe of a great multitude, so as not to declare boldly before them:) and if too I permitted a poor man to go out of my door with an empty bosom:
verses.35: (Oh that I had a hearer,) and if I had not feared the hand of the Lord; and as to the written charge which I had against any one,
verses.36: I would place it as a chaplet on my shoulders, and read it.
verses.37: And if I did not read it and return it, having taken nothing from the debtor:
verses.38: If at any time the land groaned against me, and if its furrows mourned together;
verses.39: and if I ate its strength alone without price, and if too I grieved the heart of the owner of the soil, by taking aught from him:
verses.40: then let the nettle come up to me instead of wheat, and a bramble instead of barley. And Job ceased speaking.

verses.1: Furthermore Elihu answered and said,
verses.2: Hear my words, O ye wise men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.
verses.3: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.
verses.4: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good.
verses.5: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.
verses.6: Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.
verses.7: What man is like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?
verses.8: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.
verses.9: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.
verses.10: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
verses.11: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
verses.12: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
verses.13: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?
verses.14: If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;
verses.15: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.
verses.16: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.
verses.17: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?
verses.18: Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly?
verses.19: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.
verses.20: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.
verses.21: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.
verses.22: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
verses.23: For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.
verses.24: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.
verses.25: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
verses.26: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
verses.27: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:
verses.28: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.
verses.29: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:
verses.30: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.
verses.31: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:
verses.32: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.
verses.33: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.
verses.34: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.
verses.35: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.
verses.36: My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men.
verses.37: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἐλιοὺς, λέγει,
verses.2: Ἀκούσατέ μου σοφοὶ, ἐπιστάμενοι ἐνωτίζεσθε.
verses.3: Ὅτι οὖς λόγους δοκιμάζει, καὶ λάρυγξ γεύεται βρῶσιν.
verses.4: Κρίσιν ἑλώμεθα ἑαυτοῖς, γνῶμεν ἀναμέσον ἑαυτῶν, ὅ, τι καλόν.
verses.5: Ὅτι εἴρηκεν Ἰὼβ, δίκαιός εἰμι· ὁ Κύριος ἀπήλλαξέ μου τὸ κρίμα.
verses.6: Ἐψεύσατο δὲ τῷ κρίματί μου, βίαιον τὸ βέλος μου ἄνευ ἀδικίας.
verses.7: Τίς ἀνὴρ ὥσπερ Ἰὼβ, πίνων μυκτηρισμὸν ὥσπερ ὕδωρ;
verses.8: Οὐχ ἁμαρτῶν οὐδὲ ἀσεβήσας, ἢ οὐδʼ οὐ κοινωνήσας μετὰ ποιούντων τὰ ἄνομα, τοῦ πορευθῆναι μετὰ ἀσεβῶν.
verses.9: Μὴ γὰρ εἴπῃς, ὅτι οὐκ ἔσται ἐπισκοπὴ ἀνδρός, καὶ ἐπισκοπὴ αὐτῷ παρὰ Κυρίου.
verses.10: Διὸ συνετοὶ καρδίας ἀκούσατέ μου, μή μοι εἴη ἔναντι Κυρίου ἀσεβῆσαι, καὶ ἔναντι παντοκράτορος ταράξαι τὸ δίκαιον.
verses.11: Ἀλλὰ ἀποδιδοῖ ἀνθρώπῳ καθὰ ποιεῖ ἕκαστος αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐν τρίβῳ ἀνδρὸς εὑρήσει αὐτόν.
verses.12: Οἴει δὲ τὸν Κύριον ἄτοπα ποιήσειν, ἢ ὁ παντοκράτωρ ταράξει κρίσιν,
verses.13: ὃς ἐποίησε τὴν γῆν; Τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ὑπʼ οὐρανὸν, καὶ τὰ ἐνόντα πάντα;
verses.14: Εἰ γὰρ βούλοιτο συνέχειν, καὶ τὸ σνεῦμα παρʼ αὐτῷ κατασχεῖν,
verses.15: τελευτήσει πᾶσα σὰρξ ὁμοθυμαδὸν, πᾶς δὲ βροτὸς εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσεται, ὅθεν καὶ ἐπλάσθη.
verses.16: Ἴδὲ μὴ νουθετῇ, ἄκουε ταῦτα, ἐνωτίζου φωνὴν ῥημάτων.
verses.17: Ἴδε σὺ τὸν μισοῦντα ἄνομα, καὶ τὸν ὀλλύντα τοὺς πονηροὺς, ὄντα αἰώνιον δίκαιον.
verses.18: Ἀσεβὴς ὁ λέγων βασιλεῖ, παρανομεῖς, ἀσεβέστατε τοῖς ἄρχουσιν.
verses.19: Ὃς οὐκ ἐπαισχυνθῇ πρόσωπον ἐντίμου, οὐδὲ οἶδε τιμὴν θέσθαι ἁδροῖς θαυμασθῆναι πρόσωπα αὐτῶν.
verses.20: Κενὰ δὲ αὐτοῖς ἀποβήσεται, τὸ κεκραγέναι καὶ δεῖσθαι ἀνδρός· ἐχρήσαντο γὰρ παρανόμως, ἐκκλινομένων ἀδυνάτων.
verses.21: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁρατής ἐστιν ἔργων ἀνθρώπων, λέληθε δὲ αὐτὸν οὐδὲν ὧν πράσσουσιν.
verses.22: Οὐδὲ ἔσται τόπος τοῦ κρυβῆναι τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὰ ἄνομα·
verses.23: Ὅτι οὐκ ἐπʼ ἄνδρα θήσει ἔτι.
verses.24: Ὁ γὰρ Κύριος πάντας ἐφορᾷ· ὁ καταλαμβάνων ἀνεξιχνίαστα, ἔνδοξά τε καὶ ἐξαίσια, ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός.
verses.25: Ὁ γνωρίζων αὐτῶν τὰ ἔργα, καὶ στρέψει νύκτα καὶ ταπεινωθήσοται.
verses.26: Ἔσβεσε δὲ ἀσεβεῖς, ὁρατοὶ δὲ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ.
verses.27: Ὅτι ἐξέκλιναν ἐκ νόμου Θεοῦ, δικαιώματα δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν,
verses.28: τοῦ ἐπαγαγεῖν ἐπʼ αὐτὸν κραυγὴν πενήτων, καὶ κραυγὴν πτωχῶν εἰσακούσεται.
verses.29: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἡσυχίαν παρέξει, καὶ τίς καταδικάσεται; καὶ κρύψει πρόσωπον, καὶ τίς ὄψεται αὐτόν; καὶ κατὰ ἔθνους, καὶ κατὰ ἀνθρώπου ὁμοῦ.
verses.30: Βασιλεύων ἀνθρωπον ὑποκριτὴν ἀπὸ δυσκολίας λαοῦ.
verses.31: Ὅτι πρὸς τὸν ἰσχυρὸν ὁ λέγων, εἴληφα, οὐκ ἐνεχυράσω·
verses.32: Ἄνευ ἐμαυτοῦ ὄψομαι· σὺ δεῖξόν μοι, εἰ ἀδικίαν εἰργασάμην, οὐ μὴ προσθήσω.
verses.33: Μὴ ἀπὸ σοῦ ἀποτίσει αὐτὴν, ὅτι σὺ ἀπώσῃ; ὅτι σὺ ἐκλέξῃ καὶ οὐκ ἐγώ; καὶ τί ἔγνως, λάλησον.
verses.34: Διὸ συνετοὶ καρδίας ἐροῦσι ταῦτα, ἀνὴρ δὲ σοφὸς ἀκήκοέ μου τὸ ῥῆμα.
verses.35: Ἰὼβ δὲ οὐκ ἐν συνέσει ἐλάλησε, τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐν ἐπιστήμῃ.
verses.36: Οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ μάθε Ἰώβ, μὴ δῷς ἔτι ἀνταπόκρισιν ὥσπερ οἱ ἄφρονες·
verses.37: Ἵνα μὴ προσθῶμεν ἐφʼ ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, ἀνομία δὲ ἐφʼ ἡμῖν λογισθήσεται, πολλὰ λαλούντων ῥήματα ἐναντίον τοῦ Κυρίου.

verses.1: And Elius continued, and said,
verses.2: Hear me, ye wise men; hearken, ye that have knowledge.
verses.3: For the ear tries words, and the mouth tastes meat.
verses.4: Let us choose judgment to ourselves: let us know among ourselves what is right.
verses.5: For Job has said, I am righteous: the Lord has removed my judgment.
verses.6: And he has erred in my judgment: my wound is severe without unrighteousness of mine.
verses.7: What man is as Job, drinking scorning like water?
verses.8: saying, I have not sinned, nor committed ungodliness, nor had fellowship with workers of iniquity, to go with the ungodly.
verses.9: For thou shouldest not say, There shall be no visitation of a man, whereas there is a visitation on him from the Lord.
verses.10: Wherefore hear me, ye that are wise in heart: far be it from me to sin before the Lord, and to pervert righteousness before the Almighty.
verses.11: Yea, he renders to a man accordingly as each of them does, and in a man's path he will find him.
verses.12: And thinkest thou that the Lord will do wrong, or will the Almighty who made the earth wrest judgment?
verses.13: And who is he that made the whole world under heaven, and all things therein?
verses.14: For if he would confine, and restrain his spirit with himself;
verses.15: all flesh would die together, and every mortal would return to the earth, whence also he was formed.
verses.16: Take heed lest he rebuke thee: hear this, hearken to the voice of words.
verses.17: Behold then the one that hates iniquities, and that destroys the wicked, who is for ever just.
verses.18: He is ungodly that says to a king, Thou art a transgressor, that says to princes, O most ungodly one.
verses.19: Such a one as would not reverence the face of an honourable man, neither knows how to give honour to the great, so as that their persons should be respected.
verses.20: But it shall turn out vanity to them, to cry and beseech a man; for they dealt unlawfully, the poor being turned aside from their right.
verses.21: For he surveys the works of men, and nothing of what they do has escaped him.
verses.22: Neither shall there be a place for the workers of iniquity to hide themselves.
verses.23: For he will not lay upon a man more than right.
verses.24: For the Lord looks down upon all men, who comprehends unsearchable things, glorious also and excellent things without number.
verses.25: Who discovers their works, and will bring night about upon them, and they shall be brought low.
verses.26: And he quite destroys the ungodly, for they are seen before him.
verses.27: Because they turned aside from the law of God, and did not regard his ordinances,
verses.28: so as to bring before him the cry of the needy; for he will hear the cry of the poor.
verses.29: And he will give quiet, and who will condemn? and he will hide his face, and who shall see him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man also:
verses.30: causing a hypocrite to be king, because of the waywardness of the people.
verses.31: For there is one that says to the Mighty One, I have received blessings; I will not take a pledge:
verses.32: I will see apart from myself: do thou shew me if I have done unrighteousness; I will not do so any more.
verses.33: Will he take vengeance for it on thee, whereas thou wilt put it far from thee? for thou shalt choose, and not I; and what thou knowest, speak thou.
verses.34: Because the wise in heart shall say this, and a wise man listens to my word.
verses.35: But Job has not spoken with understanding, his words are not uttered with knowledge.
verses.36: Howbeit do thou learn, Job: no longer make answer as the foolish:
verses.37: that we add not to our sins: for iniquity will be reckoned against us, if we speak many words before the Lord.

verses.1: Elihu spake moreover, and said,
verses.2: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God’s?
verses.3: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?
verses.4: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.
verses.5: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.
verses.6: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?
verses.7: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?
verses.8: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.
verses.9: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.
verses.10: But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;
verses.11: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?
verses.12: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.
verses.13: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.
verses.14: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him.
verses.15: But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity:
verses.16: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.

verses.1: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἐλιοὺς, λέγει,
verses.2: Τί τοῦτο ἡγήσω ἐν κρίσει; σὺ τίς εἶ, ὅτι εἶπας, δίκαιός εἰμι ἔναντι Κυρίου;
verses.4: Ἐγώ σοι δώσω ἀπόκρισιν, καὶ τοῖς τρισὶ φίλοις σου.
verses.5: Ἀνάβλεψον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, καὶ ἴδε· κατάμαθε δὲ νέφη, ὡς ὑψηλὰ ἀπὸ σοῦ.
verses.6: Εἰ ἥμαρτες, τί πράξεις; εἰ δὲ καὶ πολλὰ ἠνόμησας, τί δύνασαι ποιῆσαι;
verses.7: Ἐπεὶ δὲ οὖν δίκαιος εἶ, τί δώσεις αὐτῷ; ἢ τί ἐκ χειρός σου λήψεται;
verses.8: Ἀνδρὶ τῷ ὁμοίῳ σου ἡ ἀσέβειά σου, καὶ υἱῷ ἀνθρώπου ἡ δικαιοσύνη σου.
verses.9: Ἀπὸ πλήθους συκοφαντούμενοι κεκράξονται, βοήσονται ἀπὸ βραχίονος πολλῶν.
verses.10: Καὶ οὐκ εἶπε, ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας με, ὁ κατατάσσων φυλακὰς νυκτερινὰς,
verses.11: ὁ διορίζων με ἀπὸ τετραπόδων γῆς, ἀπὸ δὲ πετεινῶν οὐρανοῦ;
verses.12: Ἐκεῖ κεκράξονται, καὶ οὐ μὴ εἰσακούσῃ, καὶ ἀπὸ ὕβρεως πονηρῶν.
verses.13: Ἄτοπα γὰρ οὐ βούλεται ἰδεῖν ὁ Κύριος, αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ παντοκράτωρ.
verses.14: Ὁρατής ἐστι τῶν συντελούντων τὰ ἄνομα, καὶ σώσει με· κρίθητι δὲ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ, εἰ δύνασαι αὐτὸν αἰνέσαι, ὡς ἔστι καὶ νῦν.
verses.15: “Ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπισκεπτόμενος ὀργὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνω παράπτωμά τι σφόδρα·
verses.16: καὶ Ἰὼβ ματαίως ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ, ἐν ἀγνωσίᾳ ῥήματα βαρύνει.

verses.1: And Elius resumed and said,
verses.2: What is this that thou thinkest to be according to right? who art thou that thou hast said, I am righteous before the Lord?
verses.4: I will answer thee, and thy three friends.
verses.5: Look up to the sky and see; and consider the clouds, how high they are above thee.
verses.6: If thou hast sinned, what wilt thou do? and if too thou hast transgressed much, what canst thou perform?
verses.7: And suppose thou art righteous, what wilt thou give him? or what shall he receive of thy hand?
verses.8: Thy ungodliness may affect a man who is like to thee; or thy righteousness a son of man.
verses.9: They that are oppressed of a multitude will be ready to cry out; they will call for help because of the arm of many.
verses.10: But none said, Where is God that made me, who appoints the night-watches;
verses.11: who makes me to differ from the four-footed beasts of the earth, and from the birds of the sky?
verses.12: There they shall cry, and none shall hearken, even because of the insolence of wicked men.
verses.13: For the Lord desires not to look on error, for he is the Almighty One.
verses.14: He beholds them that perform lawless deeds, and he will save me: and do thou plead before him, if thou canst praise him, as it is possible even now.
verses.15: For he is not now regarding his wrath, nor has he noticed severely any trespass.
verses.16: Yet Job vainly opens his mouth, in ignorance he multiplies words.

verses.1: Elihu also proceeded, and said,
verses.2: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on God’s behalf.
verses.3: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
verses.4: For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.
verses.5: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.
verses.6: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.
verses.7: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.
verses.8: And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction;
verses.9: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.
verses.10: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.
verses.11: If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
verses.12: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.
verses.13: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.
verses.14: They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.
verses.15: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.
verses.16: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.
verses.17: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee.
verses.18: Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.
verses.19: Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
verses.20: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.
verses.21: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.
verses.22: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?
verses.23: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?
verses.24: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.
verses.25: Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.
verses.26: Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
verses.27: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:
verses.28: Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly.
verses.29: Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?
verses.30: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.
verses.31: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.
verses.32: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt.
verses.33: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.

verses.1: Προσθεὶς δὲ ἔτι Ἐλιοὺς, λέγει,
verses.2: Μεῖνόν με μικρὸν ἔτι, ἵνα διδάξω σε· ἔτι γὰρ ἐν ἐμοί ἐστι λέξις.
verses.3: Ἀναλαβὼν τὴν ἐπιστήμην μου μακράν, ἔργοις δέ μου δίκαια ἐρῶ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας,
verses.4: καὶ οὐκ ἄδικα ῥήματα ἀδίκως συνιεῖς.
verses.5: Γίνωσκε δὲ, ὅτι ὁ Κύριος οὐ μὴ ἀποποιήσηται τὸν ἄκακον, δυνατὸς ἰσχύϊ καρδίας
verses.6: ἀσεβῆ οὐ μὴ ζωοποιήσῃ, καὶ κρίμα πτωχῶν δώσει.
verses.7: Οὐκ ἀφελεῖ ἀπὸ δικαίου ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετὰ βασιλέων εἰς θρόνον, καὶ καθιεῖ αὐτοὺς εἰς νῖκος, καὶ ὑψωθήσονται.
verses.8: Καὶ οἱ πεπεδημένοι ἐν χειροπέδαις, συσχεθήσονται ἐν σχοινίοις πενίας.
verses.9: Καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἰσχύσουσιν.
verses.10: Ἀλλὰ τοῦ δικαίου εἰσακούσεται· καὶ εἶπεν ὅτι ἐπιστραφήσονται ἐξ ἀδικίας.
verses.11: Ἐὰν ἀκούσωσι, καὶ δουλεύσωσι, συντελέσουσι τὰς ἡμέρας αὐτῶν ἐν ἀγαθοῖς, καὶ τὰ ἔτη αὐτῶν ἐν εὐπρεπείαις.
verses.12: Ἀσεβεῖς δὲ οὐ διασώζει, παρὰ τὸ μὴ βούλεσθαι αὐτοὺς εἰδέναι τὸν Κύριον, καὶ διότι νουθετούμενοι ἀνήκοοι ἦσαν.
verses.13: Καὶ ὑποκριταὶ καρδίᾳ τάξουσι θυμόν, οὐ βοήσονται, ὅτι ἔδησεν αὐτούς.
verses.14: Ἀποθάνοι τοίνυν ἐν νεότητι ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτῶν, ἡ δὲ ζωὴ αὐτῶν τιτρωσκομένη ὑπὸ ἀγγέλων,
verses.15: ἀνθʼ ὧν ἔθλιψαν ἀσθενῆ καὶ ἀδύνατον, κρίμα δὲ πραέων ἐκθήσει.
verses.16: Καὶ προσεπιηπάτησέ σε ἐκ στόματος ἐχθροῦ, ἄβυσσος κατάχυσις ὑποκάτω αὐτῆς, καὶ κατέβη τράπεζά σου πλήρης πιότητος.
verses.17: Οὐχ ὑστερήσει δὲ ἀπὸ δικαίων κρίμα,
verses.18: θυμὸς δὲ ἐπʼ ἀσεβεῖς ἔσται, διʼ ἀσέβειαν δώρων ὧν ἐδέχοντο ἐπʼ ἀδικίαις.
verses.19: Μή σε ἐκκλινάτω ἑκὼν ὁ νοῦς δεήσεως ἐν ἀνάγκῃ ὄντων ἀδυνάτων,
verses.20: καὶ πάντας τοὺς κραταιοῦντας ἰσχὺν μὴ ἐξελκύσῃς τὴν νύκτα, τοῦ ἀναβῆναι λαοὺς ἀντʼ αὐτῶν,
verses.21: ἀλλὰ φύλαξαι μὴ πράξῃς ἄτοκα· ἐπὶ τοὺτων γὰρ ἐξείλω ἀπὸ πτωχείας.
verses.22: Ἰδοὺ ὁ ἰσχυρὸς κραταιώσει ἐν ἰσχύι αὐτοῦ· τίς γάρ ἐστι κατʼ αὐτὸν δυνάστης;
verses.23: Τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ ἐτάζων αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα; ἢ τίς ὁ εἰπὼν, ἔπραξεν ἄδικα;
verses.24: Μνήσθητι, ὅτι μεγάλα ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα, ὧν ἦρξαν ἄνδρες.
verses.25: Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος εἶδεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, ὅσοι τιτρωσκόμενοί εἰσι βροτοί.
verses.26: Ἰδοὺ ὁ ἰσχυρὸς πολύς, καὶ οὐ γνωσόμεθα· ἀριθμὸς ἐτῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπέραντος.
verses.27: Ἀριθμηταὶ δὲ αὐτῷ σταγόνες ὑετοῦ, καὶ ἐπιχυθήσονται ὑετῷ εἰς νεφέλην.
verses.28: Ῥυήσονται παλαιώματα, ἐσκίασε δὲ νέφη ἐπὶ ἀμυθήτῳ βροτῷ·
verses.28a: ὥραν ἔθετο κτήνεσιν, οἴδασι δὲ κοίτης τάξιν·
verses.28b: ἐπὶ τούτοις πᾶσιν οὐκ ἐξίσταταί σου ἡ διάνοια, οὐδὲ διαλλάσσεταί σου ἡ καρδία ἀπὸ σώματος.
verses.29: Καὶ ἐὰν συνῇ ἐπεκτάσεις νεφέλης, ἰσότητα σκηνῆς αὐτοῦ,
verses.30: ἰδοὺ ἐκτενεῖ ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἠδὼ, καὶ ῥιζώματα τῆς θαλάσσης ἐκάλυψεν.
verses.31: Ἐν γὰρ αὐτοῖς κρινεῖ λαούς, δώσει τροφὴν τῷ ἰσχύοντι.
verses.32: Ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἐκάλυψε φῶς, καὶ ἐνετείλατο περὶ αὐτῆς ἐν ἀπαντῶντι.
verses.33: Ἀναγγελεῖ περὶ αὐτοῦ φίλον αὐτοῦ Κύριος, κτῆσι καὶ περὶ ἀδικίας.

verses.1: And Elius further continued, and said,
verses.2: Wait for me yet a little while, that I may teach thee: for there is yet speech in me.
verses.3: Having fetched my knowledge from afar, and according to my works,
verses.4: I will speak just things truly, and thou shalt not unjustly receive unjust words.
verses.5: But know that the Lord will not cast off an innocent man: being mighty in strength of wisdom,
verses.6: he will not by any means save alive the ungodly: and he will grant the judgment of the poor.
verses.7: He will not turn away his eyes from the righteous, but they shall be with kings on the throne: and he will establish them in triumph, and they shall be exalted.
verses.8: But they that are bound in fetters shall be holden in cords of poverty.
verses.9: And he shall recount to them their works, and their transgressions, for such will act with violence.
verses.10: But he will hearken to the righteous: and he has said that they shall turn from unrighteousness.
verses.11: If they should hear and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in honour.
verses.12: But he preserves not the ungodly; because they are not willing to know the Lord, and because when reproved they were disobedient.

verses.1: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?
verses.2: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
verses.3: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.
verses.4: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.
verses.5: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?
verses.6: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.
verses.7: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.
verses.8: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.
verses.9: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?
verses.10: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?
verses.11: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?
verses.12: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?
verses.13: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?
verses.14: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,
verses.15: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.
verses.16: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;
verses.17: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.
verses.18: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.
verses.19: Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?
verses.20: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.
verses.21: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.
verses.22: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.
verses.23: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.
verses.24: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.
verses.25: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
verses.26: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south?
verses.27: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?
verses.28: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.
verses.29: From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.
verses.30: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.

verses.1: Why standest thou afar off, O LORD? why hidest thou thyself in times of trouble?
verses.2: The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined.
verses.3: For the wicked boasteth of his heart’s desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the LORD abhorreth.
verses.4: The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.
verses.5: His ways are always grievous; thy judgments are far above out of his sight: as for all his enemies, he puffeth at them.
verses.6: He hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved: for I shall never be in adversity.
verses.7: His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud: under his tongue is mischief and vanity.
verses.8: He sitteth in the lurking places of the villages: in the secret places doth he murder the innocent: his eyes are privily set against the poor.
verses.9: He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor: he doth catch the poor, when he draweth him into his net.
verses.10: He croucheth, and humbleth himself, that the poor may fall by his strong ones.
verses.11: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see it.
verses.12: Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up thine hand: forget not the humble.
verses.13: Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? he hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require it.
verses.14: Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless.
verses.15: Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man: seek out his wickedness till thou find none.
verses.16: The LORD is King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land.
verses.17: LORD, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear:
verses.18: To judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may no more oppress.

verses.1: Εἰς τὸ τέλος, ὑπὲρ τῶν κρυφίων τοῦ υἱοῦ, ψαλμὸς τῷ Δαυίδ.

verses.5: Ὅτι ἐποίησας τὴν κρίσιν μου καὶ τὴν δίκην μου, ἐκάθισας ἐπὶ θρόνου ὁ κρίνων δικαιοσύνην.
verses.6: Ἐπετίμησας ἔθνεσι, καὶ ἀπώλετο ὁ ἀσεβὴς· τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῶν ἐξήλειψας εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος.
verses.7: Τοῦ ἐχθροῦ ἐξέλιπον αἱ ῥομφαῖαι εἰς τέλος, καὶ πόλεις καθεῖλες· ἀπώλετο τὸ μνημόσυνον αὐτῶν μετʼ ἤχου,
verses.8: καὶ ὁ Κύριος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα μένει· ἡτοίμασεν ἐν κρίσει τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ,
verses.9: καὶ αὐτὸς κρινεῖ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, κρινεῖ λαοὺς ἐν εὐθύτητι.

verses.12: Ψάλατε τῷ Κυρίῳ τῷ κατοικοῦντι ἐν Σιὼν, ἀναγγείλατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι τὰ ἐπιτηδεύματα αὐτοῦ.

verses.15: Ὅπως ἂν ἐξαγγείλω πάσας τὰς αἰνέσεις σου ἐν ταῖς πύλαις τῆς θυγατρὸς Σιών· ἀγαλλιάσομαι ἐπὶ τῷ σωτηρίῳ σου.
verses.16: Ἐνεπάγησαν ἔθνη ἐν διαφθορᾷ ᾗ ἐποίησαν· ἐν παγίδι ταύτῃ ᾗ ἔκρυψαν συνελήφθη ὁ ποὺς αὐτῶν.
verses.17: Γινώσκεται Κύριος κρίματα ποιῶν, ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ συνελήφθη ὁ ἁμαρτωλός· ᾠδὴ διαψάλματος.

verses.19: Ὅτι οὐκ εἰς τέλος ἐπιλησθήσεται ὁ πτωχὸς, ἡ ὑπομονὴ τῶν πενήτων οὐκ ἀπολεῖται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
verses.20: Ἀνάστηθι Κύριε, μὴ κραταιούσθω ἄνθρωπος, κριθήτωσαν ἔθνη ἐνώπιόν σου.
verses.21: Κατάστησον, Κύριε, νομοθέτην ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς, γνώτωσαν ἔθνη ὅτι ἀνθρωποί εἰσι· διάψαλμα.
verses.22: Ἱνατί, Κύριε, ἀφέστηκας μακρόθεν, ὑπερορᾷς ἐν εὐκαιρίαις, ἐν θλίψει;
verses.23: Ἐν τῷ ὑπερηφανεύεσθαι τὸν ἀσεβῆ, ἐμπυρίζεται ὁ πτωχὸς, συλλαμβάνονται ἐν διαβουλίοις οἷς διαλογίζονται.
verses.24: Ὅτι ἐπαινεῖται ὁ ἁμαρτωλὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ ἀδικῶν ἐνευλογεῖται.

verses.27: Εἶπε γὰρ ἐν καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ, οὐ μὴ σαλευθῶ ἀπὸ γενεᾶς εἰς γενεὰν ἄνευ κακοῦ.

verses.31: ταπεινώσει αὐτὸν, κύψει καὶ πεσεῖται ἐν τῷ αὐτὸν κατακυριεῦσαι τῶν πενήτων.
verses.32: Εἶπε γὰρ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ, ἐπιλέλησται ὁ Θεὸς, ἀπέστρεψε τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν εἰς τέλος.
