verses.1: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
verses.2: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
verses.3: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.
verses.4: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
verses.5: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
verses.6: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?
verses.7: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear thou God.
verses.8: ¶ If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.
verses.9: ¶ Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.
verses.10: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
verses.11: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?
verses.12: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
verses.13: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.
verses.14: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
verses.15: As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
verses.16: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?
verses.17: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.
verses.18: ¶ Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it is his portion.
verses.19: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.
verses.20: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth him in the joy of his heart.

verses.1: Μὴ σπεῦδε ἐπὶ στόματί σου, καὶ καρδία σου μὴ ταχυνάτω τοῦ ἐξενέγκαι λόγον πρὸ προσώπου τοῦ Θεοῦ· ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω, καὶ σὺ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· διὰ τοῦτο ἔστωσαν οἱ λόγοι σου ὀλίγοι.
verses.2: Ὅτι παραγίνεται ἐνύπνιον ἐν πλήθει πειρασμοῦ, καὶ φωνὴ ἄφρονος ἐν πλήθει λόγων.
verses.3: Καθὼς εὔξῃ εὐχὴν τῷ Θεῷ, μὴ χρονίσῃς τοῦ ἀποδοῦναι αὐτήν· ὅτι οὐκ ἔστι θέλημα ἐν ἄφροσι· σὺ οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν εὔξῃ, ἀπόδος.
verses.4: Ἀγαθὸν τὸ μὴ εὔξασθαί σε, ἢ τὸ εὔξασθαί σε καὶ μὴ ἀποδοῦναι.
verses.5: Μὴ δῷς τὸ στόμα σου τοῦ ἐξαμαρτῆσαι τὴν σάρκα σου, καὶ μὴ εἴπῃς πρὸ προσώπου τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὅτι ἄγνοιά ἐστιν· ἵνα μὴ ὀργισθῇ ὁ Θεὸς ἐπὶ φωνῇ σου, καὶ διαφθείρῃ τὰ ποιήματα χειρῶν σου.
verses.6: Ὅτι ἐν πλήθει ἐνυπνίων καὶ ματαιοτήτων καὶ λόγων πολλῶν, ὅτι σὺ τὸν Θεὸν φοβοῦ.
verses.7: Ἐὰν συκοφαντίαν πένητος καὶ ἁρπαγὴν κρίματος καὶ δικαιοσύνης ἴδῃς ἐν χώρᾳ, μὴ θαυμάσῃς ἐπὶ τῷ πράγματι· ὅτι ὑψηλὸς ἐπάνω ὑψηλοῦ φυλάξαι, καὶ ὑψηλοὶ ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς.
verses.8: Καὶ περίσσεια γῆς ἐπὶ παντί ἐστι, βασιλεὺς τοῦ ἀγροῦ εἰργασμένου.
verses.9: Ἀγαπῶν ἀργύριον οὐ πλησθήσεται ἀργυρίου· καὶ τίς ἠγάπησεν ἐν πλήθει αὐτῶν γέννημα; καί γε τοῦτο ματαιότης.
verses.10: Ἐν πλήθει ἀγαθωσύνης ἐπληθύνθησαν ἔσθοντες αὐτήν· καὶ τί ἀνδρεία τῷ παρʼ αὐτῆς; ὅτι ἀρχὴ τοῦ ὁρᾷν ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ.
verses.11: Γλυκὺς ὕπνος τοῦ δούλου εἰ ὀλίγον καὶ εἰ πολὺ φάγεται, καὶ τῷ ἐμπλησθέντι τοῦ πλουτῆσαι, οὐκ ἔστιν ἀφίων αὐτὸν τοῦ ὑπνῶσαι.
verses.12: Ἔστιν ἀῤῥωστία ἣν εἶδον ὑπὸ τὸν ἥλιον, πλοῦτον φυλασσόμενον τῷ παρʼ αὐτοῦ εἰς κακίαν αὐτῷ,
verses.13: καὶ ἀπολεῖται ὁ πλοῦτος ἐκεῖνος ἐν περισπασμῷ πονηρῷ, καὶ ἐγέννησεν υἱὸν, καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ οὐδέν.
verses.14: Καθὼς ἐξῆλθεν ἀπὸ γαστρὸς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ γυμνὸς, ἐπιστρέψει τοῦ πορευθῆναι ὡς ἥκει, καὶ οὐδὲν οὐ λήψεται ἐν μόχθῳ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα πορευθῇ ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.15: Καί γε τοῦτο πονηρὰ ἀῤῥωστία· ὥσπερ γὰρ παρεγένετο, οὕτως καὶ ἀπελεύσεται· καὶ τίς ἡ περίσσεια αὐτοῦ ᾗ μοχθεῖ εἰς ἄνεμον;
verses.16: Καί γε πᾶσαι αἱ ἡμέραι αὐτοῦ ἐν σκότει, καὶ ἐν πένθει, καὶ θυμῷ πολλῷ, καὶ ἀῤῥωστίᾳ, καὶ χόλῳ.
verses.17: Ἰδοὺ, εἶδον ἐγὼ ἀγαθὸν, ὅ ἐστι καλὸν, τοῦ φαγεῖν καὶ τοῦ πιεῖν καὶ τοῦ ἰδεῖν ἀγαθωσύνην ἐν παντὶ μόχθῳ αὐτοῦ, ᾧ ἐὰν μοχθῇ ὑπὸ τὸν ἥλιον ἀριθμὸν ἡμερῶν ζωῆς αὐτοῦ ὧν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς, ὅτι αὐτὸ μερὶς αὐτοῦ.
verses.18: Καί γε πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ᾧ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς πλοῦτον καὶ ὑπάρχοντα, καὶ ἐξουσίασεν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ λαβεῖν τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ, καὶ τοῦ· εὐφρανθῆναι ἐν μόχθῳ αὐτοῦ, τοῦτο δόμα Θεοῦ ἐστιν.
verses.19: Ὅτι οὐ πολλὰ μνησθήσεται τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς περισπᾷ αὐτὸν ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ καρδίας αὐτοῦ.

verses.1: Be not hasty with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be swift to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven above, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
verses.2: For through the multitude of trial a dream comes; and a fool's voice is with a multitude of words.
verses.3: Whenever thou shalt vow a vow to God, defer not to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay thou therefore whatsoever thou shalt have vowed.
verses.4: It is better that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
verses.5: Suffer not thy mouth to lead thy flesh to sin; and say not in the presence of God, It was an error: lest God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the works of thy hands.
verses.6: For there is evil in a multitude of dreams and vanities and many words: but fear thou God.
verses.7: If thou shouldest see the oppression of the poor, and the wresting of judgment and of justice in the land, wonder not at the matter: for there is a high one to watch over him that is high, and high ones over them.
verses.8: Also the abundance of the earth is for every one: the king is dependent on the tilled field.
verses.9: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver: and who has loved gain, in the abundance thereof? this is also vanity.
verses.10: In the multitude of good they are increased that eat it: and what virtue has the owner, but the right of beholding it with his eyes?
verses.11: The sleep of a servant is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but to one who is satiated with wealth, there is none that suffers him to sleep.
verses.12: There is an infirmity which I have seen under the sun, namely, wealth kept for its owner to his hurt.
verses.13: And that wealth shall perish in an evil trouble: and the man begets a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
verses.14: As he came forth naked from his mother's womb, he shall return back as he came, and he shall receive nothing for his labour, that it should go with him in his hand.
verses.15: And this is also an evil infirmity: for as he came, so also shall he return: and what is his gain, for which he vainly labours?
verses.16: Yea, all his days are in darkness, and in mourning, and much sorrow, and infirmity, and wrath.
verses.17: Behold, I have seen good, that it is a fine thing for a man to eat and to drink, and to see good in all his labour in which he may labour under the sun, all the number of the days of his life which God has given to him: for it is his portion.
verses.18: Yea, and as for every man to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and has given him power to eat thereof, and to receive his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.
verses.19: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; for God troubles him in the mirth of his heart.

verses.1: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
verses.2: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
verses.3: ¶ If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.
verses.4: For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.
verses.5: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this hath more rest than the other.
verses.6: ¶ Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
verses.7: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
verses.8: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?
verses.9: ¶ Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.10: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.
verses.11: ¶ Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
verses.12: For who knoweth what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

verses.1: Ἔστι πονηρία ἣν εἶδον ὑπὸ τὸν ἥλιον, καὶ πολλή ἐστιν ὑπὸ τὸν ἄνθρωπον·
verses.2: Ἀνὴρ ᾧ δώσει αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς πλοῦτον καὶ ὑπαρχοντα καὶ δόξαν, καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ὑστερῶν τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ πάντων ὧν ἐπιθυμήσει, καὶ οὐκ ἐξουσιάσει αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ φαγεῖν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ξένος φάγεται αὐτόν· τοῦτο ματαιότης καὶ ἀῤῥωστία πονηρά ἐστιν.
verses.3: Ἐὰν γεννήσῃ ἀνὴρ ἑκατόν, καὶ ἔτη πολλὰ ζήσεται, καὶ πλῆθος ὅ, τι ἔσονται αἱ ἡμέραι ἐτῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ οὐ πλησθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγαθωσύνης, καί γε ταφὴ οὐκ ἐγένετο αὐτῷ, εἶπα, ἀγαθὸν ὑπὲρ αὐτὸν τὸ ἔκτρωμα.
verses.4: Ὅτι ἐν ματαιότητι ἦλθε, καὶ ἐν σκότει πορεύεται, καὶ ἐν σκότει ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καλυφθήσεται·
verses.5: Καί γε ἥλιον οὐκ εἶδε, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνω ἀναπαύσεις, τούτῳ ὑπὲρ τοῦτον·
verses.6: Καὶ ἔζησε χιλίων ἐτῶν καθόδους, καὶ ἀγαθωσύνην οὐκ εἶδε, μὴ οὐκ εἰς τόπον ἕνα πορεύεται τὰ πάντα;
verses.7: Πᾶς μόχθος ἀνθρώπου εἰς στόμα αὐτοῦ, καί γε ἡ ψυχὴ οὐ πληρωθήσεται.
verses.8: Ὅτι περίσσεια τῷ σοφῷ ὑπὲρ τὸν ἄφρονα, διότι ὁ πένης οἶδε πορευθῆναι κατέναντι τῆς ζωῆς.
verses.9: Ἀγαθὸν ὅραμα ὀφθαλμῶν ὑπερπορευόμενον ψυχῇ· καί γε τοῦτο ματαιότης καὶ προαίρεσις πνεύματος.
verses.10: Εἰ τι ἐγένετο, ἤδη κέκληται ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐγνώσθη ὅ ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος, καὶ οὐ δυνήσεται κριθῆναι μετὰ τοῦ ἰσχυροτὲρου ὑπὲρ αὐτόν.
verses.11: Ὅτι εἰσι λόγοι πολλοὶ πληθύνοντες ματαιότητα.
verses.12: Τί περισσὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ; ὅτι τίς οἶδεν ἀγαθὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ, ἀριθμὸν ζωῆς ἡμερῶν ματαιότητος αὐτοῦ; καὶ ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ἐν σκιᾷ· ὅτι τίς ἀπαγγελεῖ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ, τί ἔσται ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ ὑπὸ τὸν ἥλιον;

verses.1: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is abundant with man:
verses.2: a man to whom God shall give wealth, and substance, and honour, and he wants nothing for his soul of all things that he shall desire, yet God shall not give him power to eat of it, for a stranger shall devour it: this is vanity, and an evil infirmity.
verses.3: If a man beget a hundred children, and live many years, yea, however abundant the days of his years shall be, yet if his soul shall not be satisfied with good, and also he have no burial; I said, An untimely birth is better than he.
verses.4: For he came in vanity, and departs in darkness, and his name shall be covered in darkness.
verses.5: Moreover he has not seen the sun, nor known rest: there is no more rest to this one than another.
verses.6: Though he has lived to the return of a thousand years, yet he has seen no good: do not all go to one place?
verses.7: All the labour of a man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite shall not be satisfied.
verses.8: For what advantage has the wise man over the fool, since even the poor knows how to walk in the direction of life?
verses.9: The sight of the eyes is better than that which wanders in soul: this is also vanity, and waywardness of spirit.
verses.10: If anything has been, its name has already been called: and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him who is stronger than he.
verses.11: For there are many things which increase vanity.
verses.12: What advantage has a man? for who knows what is good for a man in his life, during the number of the life of the days of his vanity? and he has spent them as a shadow; for who shall tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

verses.1: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.
verses.2: ¶ It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
verses.3: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
verses.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.5: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.6: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.
verses.7: ¶ Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
verses.8: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
verses.9: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
verses.10: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.
verses.11: ¶ Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.
verses.12: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.
verses.13: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?
verses.14: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
verses.15: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness.
verses.16: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?
verses.17: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?
verses.18: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.
verses.19: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.
verses.20: For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
verses.21: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:
verses.22: For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.
verses.23: ¶ All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
verses.24: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?
verses.25: I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:
verses.26: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
verses.27: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:
verses.28: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
verses.29: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.

verses.1: Ἀγαθὸν ὄνομα ὑπὲρ ἔλαιον ἀγαθὸν, καὶ ἡμέρα τοῦ θανάτου ὑπὲρ ἡμέραν γεννήσεως.
verses.2: Ἀγαθὸν πορευθῆναι εἰς οἶκον πένθους ἢ ὅτι πορευθῆναι εἰς οἶκον πότου· καθότι τοῦτο τέλος παντὸς ἀνθρώπου, καὶ ὁ ζῶν δώσει ἀγαθὸν εἰς καρδίαν αὐτοῦ.
verses.3: Ἀγαθὸν θυμὸς ὑπὲρ γέλωτα, ὅτι ἐν κακίᾳ προσώπου ἀγαθυνθήσεται καρδία.
verses.4: Καρδία σοφῶν ἐν οἴκῳ πένθους, καὶ καρδία ἀφρόνων ἐν οἴκῳ εὐφροσύνης.
verses.5: Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἀκοῦσαι ἐπιτίμησιν σοφοῦ ὑπὲρ ἄνδρα ἁκούοντα ᾆσμα ἀφρόνων.
verses.6: Ὡς φωνὴ ἀκανθῶν ὑπὸ τὸν λέβητα, οὕτως γέλως τῶν ἀφρόνων· καί γε τοῦτο ματαιότης.
verses.7: Ὅτι ἡ συκοφαντία περιφέρει σοφὸν, καὶ ἀπόλλυσι τὴν καρδίαν εὐγενείας αὐτοῦ.
verses.8: Ἀγαθὴ ἐσχάτη λόγων ὑπὲρ ἀρχὴν αὐτοῦ, ἀγαθὸν μακρόθυμος ὑπὲρ ὑψηλὸν πνεύματι.
verses.9: Μὴ σπεύσῃς ἐν πνεύματί σου τοῦ θυμοῦσθαι, ὅτι θυμὸς ἐν κόλπῳ ἀφρόνων ἀναπαύσεται.
verses.10: Μὴ εἴπῃς, τί ἐγένετο, ὅτι αἱ ἡμέραι αἱ πρότεραι ἦσαν ἀγαθαὶ ὑπὲρ ταύτας; ὅτι οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ ἐπηρώτησας περὶ τούτου.
verses.11: Ἀγαθὴ σοφία μετὰ κληρονομίας, καὶ περίσσεια τοῖς θεωροῦσι τὸν ἥλιον.
verses.12: Ὅτι ἐν σκιᾷ αὐτῆς ἡ σοφία ὡς σκιὰ ἀργυρίου, καὶ περίσσεια γνώσεως τῆς σοφίας ζωοποιήσει τὸν παρʼ αὐτῆς.
verses.13: Ἴδε τὰ ποιήματα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὅτι τίς δυνήσεται κοσμῆσαι ὃν ἂν ὁ Θεὸς διαστρέψῃ αὐτόν;
verses.14: Ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἀγαθωσύνης ζῆθι ἐν ἀγαθῷ, καὶ ἴδε ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κακίας· ἴδε, καί γε σὺν τούτῳ συμφώνως τοῦτο ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς περὶ λαλιᾶς, ἵνα μὴ εὕρῃ ἄνθρωπος ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ οὐδέν.
verses.15: Σύμπαντα εἶδον ἐν ἡμέραις ματαιότητός μου· ἐστὶ δίκαιος ἀπολλύμενος ἐν δικαίῳ αὐτοῦ, καί ἐστιν ἀσεβὴς μένων ἐν κακίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
verses.16: Μὴ γίνου δίκαιος πολὺ, μηδὲ σοφίζου περισσὰ, μή ποτε ἐκπλαγῇς.
verses.17: Μὴ ἀσεβήσῃς πολὺ, καὶ μὴ γίνου σκληρὸς, ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνῃς ἐν οὐ καιρῷ σου.
verses.18: Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἀντέχεσθαί σε ἐν τούτῳ, καί γε ἀπὸ τούτου μὴ μιάνῃς τὴν χεῖρά σου, ὅτι φοβουμένοις τὸν Θεὸν ἐξελεύσεται τὰ πάντα.
verses.19: Ἡ σοφία βοηθήσει τῷ σοφῷ ὑπὲρ δέκα ἐξουσιάζοντας τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τῇ πόλει.
verses.20: Ὅτι ἄνθρωπος οὐκ ἔστι δίκαιος ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὃς ποιήσει ἀγαθὸν καὶ οὐχ ἁμαρτήσεται.

verses.1: A good name is better than good oil; and the day of death than the day of birth.
verses.2: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the banquet house: since this is the end of every man; and the living man will apply good warning to his heart.
verses.3: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart will be made better.
verses.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.5: It is better to hear a reproof of a wise man, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.6: As the sound of thorns under a caldron, so is the laughter of fools: this is also vanity.
verses.7: For oppression makes a wise man mad, and destroys his noble heart.
verses.8: The end of a matter is better than the beginning thereof: the patient is better than the high-minded.
verses.9: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger will rest in the bosom of fools.
verses.10: Say not, What has happened, that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire in wisdom concerning this.
verses.11: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and there is an advantage by it to them that see the sun.
verses.12: For wisdom in its shadow is as the shadow of silver: and the excellence of the knowledge of wisdom will give life to him that has it.
verses.13: Behold the works of God: for who shall be able to straighten him whom God has made crooked?
verses.14: In the day of prosperity live joyfully, and consider in the day of adversity: consider, I say, God also has caused the one to agree with the other for this reason, that man should find nothing after him.
verses.15: I have seen all things in the days of my vanity: there is a just man perishing in his justice, and there is an ungodly man remaining in his wickedness.
verses.16: Be not very just; neither be very wise: lest thou be confounded.
verses.17: Be not very wicked; and be not stubborn: lest thou shouldest die before thy time.
verses.18: It is well for thee to hold fast by this; also by this defile not thine hand: for to them that fear God all things shall come forth well.
verses.19: Wisdom will help the wise man more than ten mighty men which are in the city.
verses.20: For there is not a righteous man in the earth, who will do good, and not sin.
verses.21: Also take no heed to all the words which ungodly men shall speak; lest thou hear thy servant cursing thee.
verses.22: For many times he shall trespass against thee, and repeatedly shall he afflict thine heart; for thus also hast thou cursed others.
verses.23: All these things have I proved in wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
verses.24: That which is far beyond what was, and a great depth, who shall find it out?
verses.25: I and my heart went round about to know, and to examine, and to seek wisdom, and the account of things, and to know the folly and trouble and madness of the ungodly man.
verses.26: And I find her to be, and I will pronounce to be more bitter than death the woman which is a snare, and her heart nets, who has a band in her hands: he that is good in the sight of God shall be delivered from her; but the sinner shall be caught by her.
verses.27: Behold, this have I found, said the Preacher, seeking by one at a time to find out the account,
verses.28: which my soul sought after, but I found not: for I have found one man of a thousand; but a woman in all these I have not found.
verses.29: But, behold, this have I found, that God made man upright; but they have sought out many devices. Who knows the wise? and who knows the interpretation of a saying?

verses.1: And the LORD spake unto Moses in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, saying,
verses.2: Command the children of Israel, that they give unto the Levites of the inheritance of their possession cities to dwell in; and ye shall give also unto the Levites suburbs for the cities round about them.
verses.3: And the cities shall they have to dwell in; and the suburbs of them shall be for their cattle, and for their goods, and for all their beasts.
verses.4: And the suburbs of the cities, which ye shall give unto the Levites, shall reach from the wall of the city and outward a thousand cubits round about.
verses.5: And ye shall measure from without the city on the east side two thousand cubits, and on the south side two thousand cubits, and on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits; and the city shall be in the midst: this shall be to them the suburbs of the cities.
verses.6: And among the cities which ye shall give unto the Levites there shall be six cities for refuge, which ye shall appoint for the manslayer, that he may flee thither: and to them ye shall add forty and two cities.
verses.7: So all the cities which ye shall give to the Levites shall be forty and eight cities: them shall ye give with their suburbs.
verses.8: And the cities which ye shall give shall be of the possession of the children of Israel: from them that have many ye shall give many; but from them that have few ye shall give few: every one shall give of his cities unto the Levites according to his inheritance which he inheriteth.
verses.9: ¶ And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.10: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come over Jordan into the land of Canaan;
verses.11: Then ye shall appoint you cities to be cities of refuge for you; that the slayer may flee thither, which killeth any person at unawares.
verses.12: And they shall be unto you cities for refuge from the avenger; that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.
verses.13: And of these cities which ye shall give six cities shall ye have for refuge.
verses.14: Ye shall give three cities on this side Jordan, and three cities shall ye give in the land of Canaan, which shall be cities of refuge.
verses.15: These six cities shall be a refuge, both for the children of Israel, and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them: that every one that killeth any person unawares may flee thither.
verses.16: And if he smite him with an instrument of iron, so that he die, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.17: And if he smite him with throwing a stone, wherewith he may die, and he die, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.18: Or if he smite him with an hand weapon of wood, wherewith he may die, and he die, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.19: The revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer: when he meeteth him, he shall slay him.
verses.20: But if he thrust him of hatred, or hurl at him by laying of wait, that he die;
verses.21: Or in enmity smite him with his hand, that he die: he that smote him shall surely be put to death; for he is a murderer: the revenger of blood shall slay the murderer, when he meeteth him.
verses.22: But if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or have cast upon him any thing without laying of wait,
verses.23: Or with any stone, wherewith a man may die, seeing him not, and cast it upon him, that he die, and was not his enemy, neither sought his harm:
verses.24: Then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments:
verses.25: And the congregation shall deliver the slayer out of the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, whither he was fled: and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.
verses.26: But if the slayer shall at any time come without the border of the city of his refuge, whither he was fled;
verses.27: And the revenger of blood find him without the borders of the city of his refuge, and the revenger of blood kill the slayer; he shall not be guilty of blood:
verses.28: Because he should have remained in the city of his refuge until the death of the high priest: but after the death of the high priest the slayer shall return into the land of his possession.
verses.29: So these things shall be for a statute of judgment unto you throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.30: Whoso killeth any person, the murderer shall be put to death by the mouth of witnesses: but one witness shall not testify against any person to cause him to die.
verses.31: Moreover ye shall take no satisfaction for the life of a murderer, which is guilty of death: but he shall be surely put to death.
verses.32: And ye shall take no satisfaction for him that is fled to the city of his refuge, that he should come again to dwell in the land, until the death of the priest.
verses.33: So ye shall not pollute the land wherein ye are: for blood it defileth the land: and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it.
verses.34: Defile not therefore the land which ye shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I the LORD dwell among the children of Israel.

verses.1: The word of the LORD that came to Joel the son of Pethuel.
verses.2: Hear this, ye old men, and give ear, all ye inhabitants of the land. Hath this been in your days, or even in the days of your fathers?
verses.3: Tell ye your children of it, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.
verses.4: That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.
verses.5: Awake, ye drunkards, and weep; and howl, all ye drinkers of wine, because of the new wine; for it is cut off from your mouth.
verses.6: For a nation is come up upon my land, strong, and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he hath the cheek teeth of a great lion.
verses.7: He hath laid my vine waste, and barked my fig tree: he hath made it clean bare, and cast it away; the branches thereof are made white.
verses.8: ¶ Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
verses.9: The meat offering and the drink offering is cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests, the LORD’s ministers, mourn.
verses.10: The field is wasted, the land mourneth; for the corn is wasted: the new wine is dried up, the oil languisheth.
verses.11: Be ye ashamed, O ye husbandmen; howl, O ye vinedressers, for the wheat and for the barley; because the harvest of the field is perished.
verses.12: The vine is dried up, and the fig tree languisheth; the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all the trees of the field, are withered: because joy is withered away from the sons of men.
verses.13: Gird yourselves, and lament, ye priests: howl, ye ministers of the altar: come, lie all night in sackcloth, ye ministers of my God: for the meat offering and the drink offering is withholden from the house of your God.
verses.14: ¶ Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of the LORD your God, and cry unto the LORD,
verses.15: Alas for the day! for the day of the LORD is at hand, and as a destruction from the Almighty shall it come.
verses.16: Is not the meat cut off before our eyes, yea, joy and gladness from the house of our God?
verses.17: The seed is rotten under their clods, the garners are laid desolate, the barns are broken down; for the corn is withered.
verses.18: How do the beasts groan! the herds of cattle are perplexed, because they have no pasture; yea, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
verses.19: O LORD, to thee will I cry: for the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burned all the trees of the field.
verses.20: The beasts of the field cry also unto thee: for the rivers of waters are dried up, and the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness.

verses.1: The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the LORD, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.
verses.2: Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.
verses.3: ¶ The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?
verses.4: Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the LORD.
verses.5: If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, (how art thou cut off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes?
verses.6: How are the things of Esau searched out! how are his hidden things sought up!
verses.7: All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee; they that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee: there is none understanding in him.
verses.8: Shall I not in that day, saith the LORD, even destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau?
verses.9: And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.
verses.10: ¶ For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.
verses.11: In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.
verses.12: But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress.
verses.13: Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity;
verses.14: Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.
verses.15: For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.
verses.16: For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, so shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.
verses.17: ¶ But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.
verses.18: And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the LORD hath spoken it.
verses.19: And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.
verses.20: And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath; and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.
verses.21: And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD’s.

verses.1: Hear ye now what the LORD saith; Arise, contend thou before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice.
verses.2: Hear ye, O mountains, the LORD’s controversy, and ye strong foundations of the earth: for the LORD hath a controversy with his people, and he will plead with Israel.
verses.3: O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee? testify against me.
verses.4: For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of servants; and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
verses.5: O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim unto Gilgal; that ye may know the righteousness of the LORD.
verses.6: ¶ Wherewith shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?
verses.7: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
verses.8: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
verses.9: The LORD’s voice crieth unto the city, and the man of wisdom shall see thy name: hear ye the rod, and who hath appointed it.
verses.10: ¶ Are there yet the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and the scant measure that is abominable?
verses.11: Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights?
verses.12: For the rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
verses.13: Therefore also will I make thee sick in smiting thee, in making thee desolate because of thy sins.
verses.14: Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy casting down shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt take hold, but shalt not deliver; and that which thou deliverest will I give up to the sword.
verses.15: Thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thee with oil; and sweet wine, but shalt not drink wine.
verses.16: ¶ For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and ye walk in their counsels; that I should make thee a desolation, and the inhabitants thereof an hissing: therefore ye shall bear the reproach of my people.

verses.1: Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not;
verses.2: The noise of a whip, and the noise of the rattling of the wheels, and of the pransing horses, and of the jumping chariots.
verses.3: The horseman lifteth up both the bright sword and the glittering spear: and there is a multitude of slain, and a great number of carcases; and there is none end of their corpses; they stumble upon their corpses:
verses.4: Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.
verses.5: Behold, I am against thee, saith the LORD of hosts; and I will discover thy skirts upon thy face, and I will shew the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.
verses.6: And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will set thee as a gazingstock.
verses.7: And it shall come to pass, that all they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?
verses.8: Art thou better than populous No, that was situate among the rivers, that had the waters round about it, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was from the sea?
verses.9: Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and it was infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers.
verses.10: Yet was she carried away, she went into captivity: her young children also were dashed in pieces at the top of all the streets: and they cast lots for her honourable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
verses.11: Thou also shalt be drunken: thou shalt be hid, thou also shalt seek strength because of the enemy.
verses.12: All thy strong holds shall be like fig trees with the firstripe figs: if they be shaken, they shall even fall into the mouth of the eater.
verses.13: Behold, thy people in the midst of thee are women: the gates of thy land shall be set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire shall devour thy bars.
verses.14: Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strong holds: go into clay, and tread the morter, make strong the brickkiln.
verses.15: There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off, it shall eat thee up like the cankerworm: make thyself many as the cankerworm, make thyself many as the locusts.
verses.16: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the cankerworm spoileth, and flieth away.
verses.17: Thy crowned are as the locusts, and thy captains as the great grasshoppers, which camp in the hedges in the cold day, but when the sun ariseth they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
verses.18: Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria: thy nobles shall dwell in the dust: thy people is scattered upon the mountains, and no man gathereth them.
verses.19: There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?

verses.13: Thou art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he?

verses.1: Woe to her that is filthy and polluted, to the oppressing city!
verses.2: She obeyed not the voice; she received not correction; she trusted not in the LORD; she drew not near to her God.
verses.3: Her princes within her are roaring lions; her judges are evening wolves; they gnaw not the bones till the morrow.
verses.4: Her prophets are light and treacherous persons: her priests have polluted the sanctuary, they have done violence to the law.
verses.5: The just LORD is in the midst thereof; he will not do iniquity: every morning doth he bring his judgment to light, he faileth not; but the unjust knoweth no shame.
verses.6: I have cut off the nations: their towers are desolate; I made their streets waste, that none passeth by: their cities are destroyed, so that there is no man, that there is none inhabitant.
verses.7: I said, Surely thou wilt fear me, thou wilt receive instruction; so their dwelling should not be cut off, howsoever I punished them: but they rose early, and corrupted all their doings.
verses.8: ¶ Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the LORD, until the day that I rise up to the prey: for my determination is to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour upon them mine indignation, even all my fierce anger: for all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy.
verses.9: For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD, to serve him with one consent.
verses.10: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants, even the daughter of my dispersed, shall bring mine offering.
verses.11: In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me: for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain.
verses.12: I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the LORD.
verses.13: The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.
verses.14: ¶ Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.15: The LORD hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy: the king of Israel, even the LORD, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more.
verses.16: In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem, Fear thou not: and to Zion, Let not thine hands be slack.
verses.17: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
verses.18: I will gather them that are sorrowful for the solemn assembly, who are of thee, to whom the reproach of it was a burden.
verses.19: Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee: and I will save her that halteth, and gather her that was driven out; and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame.
verses.20: At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the LORD.

verses.1: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the LORD by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, saying,
verses.2: Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, This people say, The time is not come, the time that the LORD’s house should be built.
verses.3: Then came the word of the LORD by Haggai the prophet, saying,
verses.4: Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?
verses.5: Now therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways.
verses.6: Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.
verses.7: ¶ Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways.
verses.8: Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the LORD.
verses.9: Ye looked for much, and, lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the LORD of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.
verses.10: Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit.
verses.11: And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the new wine, and upon the oil, and upon that which the ground bringeth forth, and upon men, and upon cattle, and upon all the labour of the hands.
verses.12: ¶ Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the LORD their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the LORD their God had sent him, and the people did fear before the LORD.
verses.13: Then spake Haggai the LORD’s messenger in the LORD’s message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the LORD.
verses.14: And the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the LORD of hosts, their God,
verses.15: In the four and twentieth day of the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.

verses.1: And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Darius, that the word of the LORD came unto Zechariah in the fourth day of the ninth month, even in Chisleu;

verses.6: And when ye did eat, and when ye did drink, did not ye eat for yourselves, and drink for yourselves?
verses.7: Should ye not hear the words which the LORD hath cried by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and in prosperity, and the cities thereof round about her, when men inhabited the south and the plain?

verses.11: But they refused to hearken, and pulled away the shoulder, and stopped their ears, that they should not hear.
verses.12: Yea, they made their hearts as an adamant stone, lest they should hear the law, and the words which the LORD of hosts hath sent in his spirit by the former prophets: therefore came a great wrath from the LORD of hosts.

verses.3: And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto the LORD an offering in righteousness.
verses.4: Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the LORD, as in the days of old, and as in former years.
verses.5: And I will come near to you to judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against false swearers, and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless, and that turn aside the stranger from his right, and fear not me, saith the LORD of hosts.
verses.6: For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.

verses.1: I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea:
verses.2: That ye receive her in the Lord, as becometh saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever business she hath need of you: for she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.
verses.3: Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus:
verses.4: Who have for my life laid down their own necks: unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.

verses.6: Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us.

verses.8: Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord.
verses.9: Salute Urbane, our helper in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.
verses.10: Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus’ household.
verses.11: Salute Herodion my kinsman. Greet them that be of the household of Narcissus, which are in the Lord.
verses.12: Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, which laboured much in the Lord.
verses.13: Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
verses.14: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren which are with them.
verses.15: Salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints which are with them.
verses.16: Salute one another with an holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute you.
verses.17: Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.

verses.25: Now to him that is of power to stablish you according to my gospel, and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began,
verses.26: But now is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith:

verses.1: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,
verses.2: Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours:
verses.3: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.4: I thank my God always on your behalf, for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ;
verses.5: That in every thing ye are enriched by him, in all utterance, and in all knowledge;
verses.6: Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you:
verses.7: So that ye come behind in no gift; waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ:
verses.8: Who shall also confirm you unto the end, that ye may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.9: God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.10: Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
verses.11: For it hath been declared unto me of you, my brethren, by them which are of the house of Chloe, that there are contentions among you.
verses.12: Now this I say, that every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.
verses.13: Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?
verses.14: I thank God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius;
verses.15: Lest any should say that I had baptized in mine own name.
verses.16: And I baptized also the household of Stephanas: besides, I know not whether I baptized any other.
verses.17: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect.
verses.18: For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God.
verses.19: For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.
verses.20: Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world? hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?
verses.21: For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.
verses.22: For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom:
verses.23: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness;
verses.24: But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.
verses.25: Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
verses.26: For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called:
verses.27: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;
verses.28: And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are:
verses.29: That no flesh should glory in his presence.
verses.30: But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption:
verses.31: That, according as it is written, He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.

verses.1: Moreover, brethren, we do you to wit of the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia;
verses.2: How that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.
verses.3: For to their power, I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they were willing of themselves;
verses.4: Praying us with much intreaty that we would receive the gift, and take upon us the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.
verses.5: And this they did, not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God.
verses.6: Insomuch that we desired Titus, that as he had begun, so he would also finish in you the same grace also.
verses.7: Therefore, as ye abound in every thing, in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all diligence, and in your love to us, see that ye abound in this grace also.
verses.8: I speak not by commandment, but by occasion of the forwardness of others, and to prove the sincerity of your love.
verses.9: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.
verses.10: And herein I give my advice: for this is expedient for you, who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago.
verses.11: Now therefore perform the doing of it; that as there was a readiness to will, so there may be a performance also out of that which ye have.
verses.12: For if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not.
verses.13: For I mean not that other men be eased, and ye burdened:
verses.14: But by an equality, that now at this time your abundance may be a supply for their want, that their abundance also may be a supply for your want: that there may be equality:
verses.15: As it is written, He that had gathered much had nothing over; and he that had gathered little had no lack.
verses.16: But thanks be to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.
verses.17: For indeed he accepted the exhortation; but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you.
verses.18: And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches;
verses.19: And not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind:
verses.20: Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us:
verses.21: Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
verses.22: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which I have in you.
verses.23: Whether any do enquire of Titus, he is my partner and fellowhelper concerning you: or our brethren be enquired of, they are the messengers of the churches, and the glory of Christ.
verses.24: Wherefore shew ye to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf.

verses.1: Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.

verses.3: But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:
verses.4: And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:
verses.5: To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.
verses.6: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man’s person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:
verses.7: But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;
verses.8: (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)
verses.9: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
verses.10: Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.

verses.14: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

verses.1: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,

verses.1: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
verses.2: For by it the elders obtained a good report.
verses.3: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
verses.4: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
verses.5: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.
verses.6: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
verses.7: By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
verses.8: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
verses.9: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
verses.10: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
verses.11: Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.
verses.12: Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.
verses.13: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
verses.14: For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.
verses.15: And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.
verses.16: But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.
verses.17: By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son,
verses.18: Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:
verses.19: Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.
verses.20: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
verses.21: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.
verses.22: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.
verses.23: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.
verses.24: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;
verses.25: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
verses.26: Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.
verses.27: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
verses.28: Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.
verses.29: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.
verses.30: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.
verses.31: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.
verses.32: And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:
verses.33: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
verses.34: Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.
verses.35: Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:
verses.36: And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:
verses.37: They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented;
verses.38: (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.
verses.39: And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:
verses.40: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.

verses.1: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.
verses.2: For if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;
verses.3: And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:
verses.4: Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?
verses.5: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?
verses.6: But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?
verses.7: Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?
verses.8: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:
verses.9: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.
verses.10: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
verses.11: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.
verses.12: So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.
verses.13: For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.
verses.14: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?
verses.15: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,
verses.16: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?
verses.17: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
verses.18: Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.
verses.19: Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.
verses.20: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?
verses.21: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
verses.22: Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?
verses.23: And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.
verses.24: Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.
verses.25: Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
verses.26: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

verses.1: Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives;
verses.2: While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.
verses.3: Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;
verses.4: But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.
verses.5: For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands:
verses.6: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement.
verses.7: Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.
verses.8: Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:
verses.9: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.
verses.10: For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile:
verses.11: Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.
verses.12: For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.
verses.13: And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?
verses.14: But and if ye suffer for righteousness’ sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;
verses.15: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
verses.16: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.
verses.17: For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.
verses.18: For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:
verses.19: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;
verses.20: Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.
verses.21: The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ:
verses.22: Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him.

verses.1: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained like precious faith with us through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ:
verses.2: Grace and peace be multiplied unto you through the knowledge of God, and of Jesus our Lord,
verses.3: According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue:
verses.4: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
verses.5: And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge;
verses.6: And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness;
verses.7: And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.
verses.8: For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.9: But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.
verses.10: Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall:
verses.11: For so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
verses.12: Wherefore I will not be negligent to put you always in remembrance of these things, though ye know them, and be established in the present truth.
verses.13: Yea, I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance;
verses.14: Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me.
verses.15: Moreover I will endeavour that ye may be able after my decease to have these things always in remembrance.
verses.16: For we have not followed cunningly devised fables, when we made known unto you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
verses.17: For he received from God the Father honour and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
verses.18: And this voice which came from heaven we heard, when we were with him in the holy mount.
verses.19: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:
verses.20: Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.
verses.21: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

verses.1: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life;
verses.2: (For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us;)
verses.3: That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you, that ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ.
verses.4: And these things write we unto you, that your joy may be full.
verses.5: This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.
verses.6: If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth:
verses.7: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.
verses.8: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
verses.9: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
verses.10: If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

verses.1: The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth;
verses.2: For the truth’s sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever.
verses.3: Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
verses.4: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father.
verses.5: And now I beseech thee, lady, not as though I wrote a new commandment unto thee, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.
verses.6: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.
verses.7: For many deceivers are entered into the world, who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist.
verses.8: Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.
verses.9: Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ, hath not God. He that abideth in the doctrine of Christ, he hath both the Father and the Son.
verses.10: If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed:
verses.11: For he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds.
verses.12: Having many things to write unto you, I would not write with paper and ink: but I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full.
verses.13: The children of thy elect sister greet thee. Amen.

verses.1: The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth.
verses.2: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
verses.3: For I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth.
verses.4: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
verses.5: Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers;
verses.6: Which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well:
verses.7: Because that for his name’s sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.
verses.8: We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth.
verses.9: I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.
verses.10: Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth, prating against us with malicious words: and not content therewith, neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church.
verses.11: Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.
verses.12: Demetrius hath good report of all men, and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record; and ye know that our record is true.
verses.13: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee:
verses.14: But I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name.
